title.en: Volume 84 Biographies 22: Gao Former Name Salihe, Nouwanwendunsizhong Son: Qian, Nephew: Wudai, Ang, Gao Zhen, Bai Yanjing, Zhang Jingren
title.raw: 卷八十四 列傳第二十二: 杲本名撒離喝 耨碗溫敦思忠子:謙，侄:兀帶 昂 高楨 白彥敬 張景仁 Volume 84 Biographies 22: Gao Former Name Salihe, Nouwanwendunsizhong Son: Qian, Nephew: Wudai, Ang, Gao Zhen, Bai Yanjing, Zhang Jingren

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十二 ○杲本名撒離喝 耨碗溫敦思忠子:謙，侄:兀帶 昂 高楨 白彥敬 張景仁

translations.literal: Biographies 22: Gao (original name Saliha), Nouwanwendun Sizhong; sons: Qian; nephews: Wudai, Ang, Gao Zhen, Bai Yanjing, Zhang Jingren
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 22 — Gao (born Saliha); Nouwanwendun Sizhong; his sons Qian; his nephews Wudai, Ang, Gao Zhen, Bai Yanjing, and Zhang Jingren

sentences.zh: 杲，本名撒離喝，安帝六代孫，泰州婆盧火之族，胡魯補山之子。

translations.literal: Gao, original name Saliha, sixth-generation descendant of Emperor Andi, of the Baluhuo clan of Taizhou, son of Hulubu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Gao, whose original name was Saliha, was a sixth-generation descendant of Emperor Andi, of the Baluhuo clan of Taizhou, and the son of Hulubu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 雄偉有才略，太祖愛之，常在軍中。

translations.literal: Imposing in stature and gifted in strategy, the Taizu Emperor loved him and kept him constantly with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and commanding, with a gift for strategy, he won Taizu's favor and was kept at his side on campaign.

sentences.zh: 及婆盧火為泰州都統，宗族皆隨遷泰州。

translations.literal: When Baluhuo became commander of Taizhou, the whole clan moved with him to Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Baluhuo was made commander of Taizhou, the entire clan relocated there with him.

sentences.zh: 撒離喝嘗為世祖養子，獨得不遷，仍居安出虎水。

translations.literal: Saliha had once been the Shizu Emperor's adopted son; he alone was not required to move and continued to live on the Anchuhu River.
translations.idiomatic: Because Saliha had once been Shizu's adopted son, he alone was exempt from the move and remained on the Anchuhu River.

sentences.zh: 宗翰、宗望已再克汴，執宋二主北還。

translations.literal: Zonghan and Zongwang had twice taken Bian and brought the two Song emperors north as captives.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan and Zongwang had twice captured Bianjing and marched the two Song emperors north as prisoners.

sentences.zh: 宗望分遣諸將定河北。

translations.literal: Zongwang dispatched generals to pacify Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang sent his generals out to secure Hebei.

sentences.zh: 左都監闍母攻下河間。

translations.literal: Left overseer Zhanmu attacked and took Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: The left overseer Zhanmu captured Hejian.

sentences.zh: 雄州李成棄城走，撒離喝邀擊，大破之，雄州遂降。

translations.literal: Li Cheng of Xiongzhou abandoned the city and fled; Saliha intercepted him, inflicted a great defeat, and Xiongzhou then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Cheng of Xiongzhou abandoned the city and fled, Saliha cut him off and routed his force, and Xiongzhou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 睿宗經略山東，留撒離喝於河上，而真定境內有賊眾，自稱元帥秦王。

translations.literal: The Ruizong Emperor campaigned in Shandong and left Saliha on the river, while within Zhending territory there were bandits who styled themselves Marshal and King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: While the Ruizong Emperor campaigned in Shandong, he left Saliha on the Yellow River. Within Zhending, rebels had proclaimed themselves marshal and King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 撒離喝擊破其眾，執而戮之。

translations.literal: Saliha smashed their force, seized them, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Saliha defeated them, took them prisoner, and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 從平陝西，撒離喝徇地自渭以西，降德順軍，又降涇原路鎮戎軍，進平熙河，降甘泉等三堡，遂取保川城，明年，同奔睹討平河外，降甯洮、安隴二寨，並降下河及樂州。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Shaanxi, Saliha swept the territory west of the Wei, received the surrender of Deshun Army, then of Zhenyuan Circuit's Zhenrong Army, advanced to pacify Xihé, reduced the three forts of Ganquan and others, and then took Baochuan city. The next year, together with Bendu he subdued the lands beyond the river, received the surrender of the two stockades of Ningtao and Anlong, and also received the surrender of Xiahe and Lezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign to pacify Shaanxi, Saliha marched west of the Wei, accepting the surrender of Deshun Army and then Zhenrong Army on the Jingyuan circuit. He advanced into Xihé, took three Ganquan forts, and seized Baochuan. The following year, with Bendu he subdued the territory beyond the river, winning Ningtao and Anlong stockades and the surrender of Xiahe and Lezhou.

sentences.zh: 至西寧，盡降其都護官屬，於是木波族長等皆迎降。

translations.literal: Reaching Xining, he brought all its protector and officials to surrender; thereupon the chiefs of the Mubo tribe and others all came out to welcome and submit.
translations.idiomatic: At Xining he compelled the protector and his entire staff to submit, and the Mubo chiefs and others came forward to surrender.

sentences.zh: 攻慶陽，敗其拒者，遂降其城。

translations.literal: He attacked Qingyang, defeated those who resisted, and the city then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He assaulted Qingyang, broke the defenders, and the city capitulated.

sentences.zh: 慕洧以環州來降，得城寨十三，步騎一萬。

translations.literal: Mu Wei came to surrender with Huanzhou; he gained thirteen walled towns and stockades and ten thousand infantry and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Wei surrendered Huanzhou to him, yielding thirteen fortified posts and ten thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 於是，宗弼軍敗于和尚原，上褒美撒離喝而戒勵宗弼。

translations.literal: At this time Zongbi's army was defeated at Heshangyuan; the emperor praised Saliha and admonished Zongbi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi's army was beaten at Heshangyuan, the throne praised Saliha and rebuked Zongbi.

sentences.zh: 睿宗已定陝西，留兵屯沖要，使撒離喝總之。

translations.literal: The Ruizong Emperor had already pacified Shaanxi, left troops garrisoned at strategic points, and put Saliha in overall command.
translations.idiomatic: After Ruizong had secured Shaanxi, he left troops at key posts and placed Saliha in command of them all.

sentences.zh: 居無何，請收劍外十三州。

translations.literal: Before long he requested to recover the thirteen prefectures beyond Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he asked permission to recover the thirteen prefectures south of Jian.

sentences.zh: 與宋王彥之軍七千人遇于沙會濼，敗之，遂克金州。

translations.literal: He met the seven-thousand-man army of the Song general Wang Yan at Shahui Marsh, defeated it, and then took Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He met Wang Yan's seven thousand Song troops at Shahui Marsh, routed them, and captured Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 連破吳玠諸軍于饒峰關，遂取真符縣，取洋州入興元府。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated Wu Jie's various armies at Raofeng Pass, then took Zhenfu County, took Yangzhou, and entered Xingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He broke Wu Jie's forces again and again at Raofeng Pass, seized Zhenfu County, took Yangzhou, and advanced into Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 敗吳玠兵於固鎮，擒其兩將。

translations.literal: He defeated Wu Jie's troops at Guzhen and captured two of his generals.
translations.idiomatic: At Guzhen he routed Wu Jie and took two of his commanders prisoner.

sentences.zh: 撒葛柷等破宋兵，盡下諸砦及仙人關。

translations.literal: Sagezhu and others defeated Song troops and took all the stockades and Xianren Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Sagezhu and his colleagues defeated the Song and captured every stockade along with Xianren Pass.

sentences.zh: 天會十四年，為元帥右監軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianhui he became right overseer of the marshal's command.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 14 he was made right overseer under the marshal.

sentences.zh: 天眷三年，宗弼複取河南。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjuan, Zongbi again recovered Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjuan 3, Zongbi reconquered Henan.

sentences.zh: 撒離喝自河中出陝西。

translations.literal: Saliha marched out from Hezhong into Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Saliha advanced from Hezhong into Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 既至鳳翔，擊走宋軍。

translations.literal: Having reached Fengxiang, he drove off the Song army.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang he drove the Song forces back.

sentences.zh: 是時，宋軍在京兆西者甚眾。

translations.literal: At this time Song forces west of Jingzhao were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Large Song forces still held the country west of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 諸將以暑雨，欲駐軍。

translations.literal: The generals, citing summer heat and rain, wished to halt the army.
translations.idiomatic: The generals urged a halt, citing the summer heat and rains.

sentences.zh: 且聞宋兵九萬會於涇州，都元帥遣河南步卒來會軍。

translations.literal: Moreover it was heard that ninety thousand Song troops were assembling at Jingzhou, and the supreme commander sent Henan infantry to join the army.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that ninety thousand Song troops were gathering at Jingzhou, and the supreme commander dispatched Henan foot soldiers to reinforce the army.

sentences.zh: 撒離喝留諸將屯環慶，獨以輕騎取涇州。

translations.literal: Saliha left the generals to garrison Huanqing and alone with light cavalry took Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Saliha left the other generals at Huanqing and rode ahead with a light force to seize Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，敗宋兵於涇州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he defeated Song troops at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he routed the Song at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋兵走渭州，拔離速追擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: The Song army fled toward Weizhou; Balisu pursued and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The Song fell back on Weizhou; Balisu pursued and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為右副元帥。

translations.literal: Before long he became right deputy marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made right deputy marshal.

sentences.zh: 皇統三年，封應國公，錫賚甚厚。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangtong he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ying and received very rich gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 3 he was created Duke of Ying and showered with rewards.

sentences.zh: 熙宗出獵，賜具裝馬二，命射於圍中。

translations.literal: When the Xizong Emperor went hunting, he bestowed two fully caparisoned horses and ordered him to shoot within the beat.
translations.idiomatic: On a hunt the Xizong Emperor gave him two fully equipped horses and had him shoot inside the game enclosure.

sentences.zh: 加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Bearer of the Merit Equal to the Three Dukes with the privilege of opening an office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Bearer of the Merit Equal to the Three Dukes with privilege to open an office.

sentences.zh: 將還軍，命宰臣餞之。

translations.literal: When he was about to return to the army, the emperor ordered the chief ministers to give him a farewell feast.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to return to the field, the chief ministers were ordered to send him off with a feast.

sentences.zh: 海陵升蒲州為河中府，撒離喝為河中尹，左副元帥如故。

translations.literal: Hailing raised Puzhou to Hezhong Prefecture; Saliha became prefect of Hezhong while remaining left deputy marshal as before.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing elevated Puzhou to Hezhong Prefecture and made Saliha its prefect, retaining his rank as left deputy marshal.

sentences.zh: 自陝西入朝，因從容言曰：「唐建成不道，太宗以義除之，即位之後，力行善政，後世稱賢。

translations.literal: Returning from Shaanxi to court, he spoke at leisure, saying: "In Tang, Jiancheng was without the Way; Taizong removed him on grounds of righteousness. After taking the throne he strove to practice good government, and later ages call him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from Shaanxi to court he remarked at ease: "In Tang, Jiancheng was unprincipled; Taizong removed him in the name of righteousness. Once enthroned he devoted himself to good government, and posterity calls him wise.

sentences.zh: 陛下以前主失德，大義廢絕，力行善政，則如唐太宗矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty, because the former lord lost virtue and was set aside in accordance with great righteousness, if you strive to practice good government, you will be like Tang Taizong."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty set aside the former ruler for his loss of virtue in the name of righteousness; if you now devote yourself to good government, you will stand with Tang Taizong."

sentences.zh: 海陵聞其言，色變，撒離喝亦悔其言。

translations.literal: When Hailing heard these words his countenance changed; Saliha too regretted having spoken.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing's face darkened at the words, and Saliha immediately regretted having spoken.

sentences.zh: 既而進封國王，從行官吏皆官賞之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was advanced to Prince of the State; all officials who had accompanied him were promoted and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to Prince of the State, and every official who had traveled with him was promoted and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 海陵念撒離喝久握兵在外，頗得士心，忌之，以為行台左丞相兼左副元帥。

translations.literal: Hailing, mindful that Saliha had long held command abroad and had won considerable loyalty among the troops, was jealous of him and appointed him left chief minister of the traveling secretariat while retaining him as left deputy marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing feared Saliha's long command abroad and the loyalty he had won among the soldiery, and though jealous of him, named him left chief minister of the traveling secretariat while keeping him as left deputy marshal.

sentences.zh: 又恐不奉命，陽尊以殊禮，使系屬籍，以玉帶璽書賜之。

translations.literal: Fearing he might not obey orders, he outwardly honored him with special ceremony, had him entered in the imperial clan register, and bestowed on him an imperial jade belt and sealed letter.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid Saliha might refuse to come, he showered him with outward honors, enrolled him in the clan register, and sent him an imperial jade belt and sealed letter.

sentences.zh: 撒離喝至汴，詔諭行台右丞相、右副元帥撻不野無使撒離喝預軍事。

translations.literal: When Saliha reached Bian, an edict instructed the traveling secretariat's right chief minister and right deputy marshal Tabuye not to let Saliha take part in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Saliha reached Bian, an edict told the right chief minister and right deputy marshal Tabuye to keep Saliha out of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 撒離喝不知，每事輒爭之。

translations.literal: Saliha did not know this and disputed him on every matter.
translations.idiomatic: Unaware of the order, Saliha contested him at every turn.

sentences.zh: 撻不野詭曰：「太師梁王以陝西事屬公，以河南事屬撻不野，今未嘗別奉詔命。

translations.literal: Tabuye deceptively said: "Grand Preceptor the Prince of Liang assigned Shaanxi affairs to you and Henan affairs to Tabuye; we have not yet received a separate imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Tabuye answered evasively: "Grand Preceptor the Prince of Liang left Shaanxi to you and Henan to me; no separate order has reached us.

sentences.zh: 陝西之事，撻不野固不敢干涉。」

translations.literal: As for Shaanxi affairs, Tabuye would certainly not dare to interfere."
translations.idiomatic: Matters in Shaanxi I would never presume to touch."

sentences.zh: 撻不野久在河南，將帥畏而附之。

translations.literal: Tabuye had long been in Henan, and the generals feared him and attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Tabuye had held Henan for years, and the commanders feared him and rallied to his side.

sentences.zh: 撒離喝始至勢孤，爭之不得，白於朝。

translations.literal: Saliha had only just arrived and was isolated in strength; he could not prevail in the disputes and reported to court.
translations.idiomatic: Newly arrived and without allies, Saliha could win no argument and appealed to the court.

sentences.zh: 大臣知上旨，報曰：「如梁王教。」

translations.literal: The chief ministers, knowing the emperor's intent, replied: "Do as the Prince of Liang instructs."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers, knowing the emperor's mind, answered: "Follow the Prince of Liang's direction."

sentences.zh: 及詔使至汴，諭旨於撻不野。

translations.literal: When the edict envoy reached Bian, he conveyed the imperial intent to Tabuye.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial envoy reached Bian, he delivered the order to Tabuye.

sentences.zh: 使還，撻不野獨有附奏，撒離喝不得與聞，人皆知海陵使撻不野圖之矣。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, Tabuye alone had a supplementary memorial; Saliha was not allowed to know of it. Everyone knew that Hailing had set Tabuye to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: On the envoy's return Tabuye alone filed a supplementary memorial that Saliha was not permitted to see. All understood that Hailing had set Tabuye to entrap him.

sentences.zh: 會海陵欲除遼王斜也子孫及平章政事宗義等，元帥府令史遙設希海陵旨，誣撒離喝父子謀反，並平章宗義、尚書謀裏野等。

translations.literal: It happened that Hailing wished to eliminate the descendants of the Prince of Liao Xieye and the chief councilor Zongyi and others; the marshalate clerk Yaoshe, hoping to please Hailing's intent, falsely accused Saliha father and son of plotting rebellion, together with chief councilor Zongyi, minister Moliye, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Hailing was moving against the descendants of Prince of Liao Xieye and Chief Councilor Zongyi. The marshalate clerk Yaoshe, eager to please him, framed Saliha and his son for treason, along with Zongyi, Minister Moliye, and others.

sentences.zh: 遙設學撒離喝手署及印文，詐為契丹小字家書與其子宗安，從左都監奔睹上變。

translations.literal: Yaoshe imitated Saliha's handwriting and seal, forged a Khitan small-script family letter to his son Zong'an, and through the left overseer Bendu submitted a report of treason.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoshe copied Saliha's hand and seal, forged a Khitan small-script letter to his son Zong'an, and had the left overseer Bendu lodge a treason report.

sentences.zh: 封題作已經開拆者，書紙隱約有白字，作曾經水浸，致字畫分明者，稱御史大夫宗安于宮門外遺下此書，遙設拾得之。

translations.literal: The cover was made to look already opened; the paper faintly showed white characters, as if it had once been soaked in water so that the writing now stood clear. He claimed that Censor-in-Chief Zong'an had dropped this letter outside the palace gate and that Yaoshe had picked it up.
translations.idiomatic: The envelope was made to look already opened; faint white characters showed through the paper, as if water damage had later brought the writing into relief. He claimed Censor-in-Chief Zong'an had dropped it outside the palace gate and that he had found it.

sentences.zh: 其書略曰：「撻不野自來於我不好，凡事常有堤防，應是知得上意。

translations.literal: The letter in brief said: "Tabuye has never been friendly toward me; he is always on guard in every matter — he must know the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The letter read in part: "Tabuye has always been hostile to me and watches every move — he must know what the throne intends.

sentences.zh: 移剌補丞相于我不好，若遲緩分毫，猜疑必落他手也。」

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Yila Bu is ill disposed toward me; if we delay even slightly, suspicion will surely fall into his hands."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Yila Bu is against me; the slightest delay and suspicion will pass to him."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「阿渾每見此書，約定月日，教掃胡令史卻寫白字書來。」

translations.literal: It also said: "Whenever Ahun sees this letter, set a date and have the clerk Saohu write back in white characters."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "When Ahun sees this, fix a date and have Clerk Saohu reply in white script."

sentences.zh: 有司鞫問，宗安不服曰：「使真有此書，我剖肌肉藏之，猶恐漏泄，安得于朝門下遺之？」

translations.literal: When the authorities interrogated him, Zong'an would not confess, saying: "If such a letter truly existed, I would cut open my flesh to hide it and still fear it might leak — how could I have dropped it beneath the court gate?"
translations.idiomatic: Under interrogation Zong'an refused to confess: "If I had such a letter I would cut open my flesh to hide it and still fear discovery — how could I have dropped it at the palace gate?"

sentences.zh: 有司掠笞楚毒，宗安神色不變。

translations.literal: The authorities flogged and tortured him with the utmost severity, yet Zong'an's expression did not change.
translations.idiomatic: They beat and tortured him without mercy, yet his face never changed.

sentences.zh: 乃置掃胡爐炭上，掃胡不能堪，自誣服。

translations.literal: They then placed Saohu on a brazier of coals; Saohu could not endure it and falsely confessed.
translations.idiomatic: They set Saohu on a bed of coals; unable to bear it, he confessed falsely.

sentences.zh: 宗安謂掃胡曰：「爾苦矣。」

translations.literal: Zong'an said to Saohu: "You suffer greatly."
translations.idiomatic: Zong'an told Saohu: "You have suffered enough."

sentences.zh: 宗義被掠笞，不能當，亦自誣服，曰：「我輩知不免矣，不早決，徒自苦。」

translations.literal: Zongyi was flogged and could not bear it; he too falsely confessed, saying: "We know we cannot escape; if we do not decide early, we only torment ourselves in vain."
translations.idiomatic: Zongyi, under the lash, could not endure it and also confessed falsely: "We know there is no escape; delay only prolongs our suffering."

sentences.zh: 宗安曰：「今雖無以自明，九泉之下當有冤對，吾終不能引屈。」

translations.literal: Zong'an said: "Though I cannot now clear myself, in the realm below the yellow springs there will be an accounting for this injustice; I will never yield to false confession."
translations.idiomatic: Zong'an said: "I cannot clear my name now, but in the grave there will be reckoning for this wrong; I will never plead guilty to a lie."

sentences.zh: 竟不服而死。

translations.literal: In the end he would not confess and died.
translations.idiomatic: He died without ever confessing.

sentences.zh: 使廝魯渾殺撒離喝於汴，族其家，而無寫書及傳書者主名。

translations.literal: He sent Siluhun to kill Saliha at Bian and exterminated his clan, yet there was no identification of who had written or transmitted the letter.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Siluhun to kill Saliha at Bian and wiped out his family, yet no author or courier of the letter was ever named.

sentences.zh: 有折哥者，能契丹小字，舊嘗從撒離喝。

translations.literal: There was one Zhege who knew Khitan small script and had formerly followed Saliha.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Zhege, who knew Khitan small script and had once served under Saliha.

sentences.zh: 特末者，陝西舊將，嘗以左副元帥事馳驛赴闕。

translations.literal: Teme was an old general of Shaanxi who had once ridden post-haste to court on left deputy marshal business.
translations.idiomatic: Teme was an old Shaanxi commander who had once ridden post-haste to court on left deputy marshal business.

sentences.zh: 兩人者皆族誅。

translations.literal: both men were executed together with their clans.
translations.idiomatic: Both were executed to the last of their kin.

sentences.zh: 撒離喝親屬坐是死者二十余人。

translations.literal: More than twenty of Saliha's kinsmen died on this charge.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty of Saliha's relatives died in the affair.

sentences.zh: 魯王斡者孫耶魯候撒離喝於汴，廝魯渾執之，耶魯曰：「願付有司，若法當同坐，雖死不恨。」

translations.literal: Yelu, grandson of Prince of Lu Wo, waited on Saliha at Bian; Siluhun seized him. Yelu said: "I ask to be handed over to the authorities; if the law requires that I share guilt, I shall die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: Yelu, grandson of Prince of Lu Wo, had come to wait on Saliha at Bian. Siluhun seized him, and Yelu said: "Hand me to the magistrates; if the law condemns me with him, I die without regret."

sentences.zh: 廝魯渾亦殺之。

translations.literal: Siluhun killed him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Siluhun killed him anyway.

sentences.zh: 其家訟於朝，海陵不問，但賜錢二百萬。

translations.literal: His family brought suit at court; Hailing did not investigate but only bestowed two million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: The family appealed to court; Hailing would not hear the case and merely gave them two million in cash.

sentences.zh: 奔睹遷元帥左監軍，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Bendu was transferred to left overseer of the marshal's command and advanced to Bearer of the Merit Equal to the Three Dukes with privilege to open an office.
translations.idiomatic: Bendu was made left overseer under the marshal and promoted to Bearer of the Merit Equal to the Three Dukes with privilege to open an office.

sentences.zh: 遙設為同知博州事，賜錢三百萬，謂之曰：「爾無自比老人。

translations.literal: Yaoshe was made associate prefect of Bozhou and given three million in cash. The emperor told him: "Do not compare yourself to the Old Man.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoshe was appointed associate prefect of Bozhou and given three million cash. Hailing told him: "Do not rank yourself with the Old Man.

sentences.zh: 老人親告朕，爾以告有司，設有撒離喝黨人在其間，敗吾事矣。」

translations.literal: The Old Man told me in person; if you report to the authorities, should any of Saliha's partisans be among them, you will ruin my affair."
translations.idiomatic: The Old Man told me himself; if you go to the magistrates, any of Saliha's faction there will ruin the whole affair."

sentences.zh: 老人指蕭玉也。

translations.literal: The Old Man" referred to Xiao Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Old Man meant Xiao Yu.

sentences.zh: 蕭玉名老人，故雲然。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu was called the Old Man, hence he spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu went by the name Old Man, which is why he spoke that way.

sentences.zh: 遙設在博州數歲，後與蕭裕謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: Yaoshe spent several years at Bozhou; later he plotted rebellion with Xiao Yu and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: After several years at Bozhou, Yaoshe joined Xiao Yu in a rebellion and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 大定初，詔複撒離喝官爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dadu reign an edict restored Saliha's offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dadu reign an edict restored Saliha's offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 三年，追封金源郡王，諡莊襄，以郡王品秩官為營葬。

translations.literal: In the third year he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jinyuan Commandery with the posthumous title Zhuangxiang, and officials of princely rank were assigned to arrange his burial.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was posthumously created Prince of Jinyuan with the temple name Zhuangxiang, and officials of princely rank were ordered to conduct his funeral.

sentences.zh: 十七年，配享太宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was given a place in the temple hall of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was granted a place in Taizong's temple.

sentences.zh: 耨碗溫敦思忠

translations.literal: Nouwanwendun Sizhong
translations.idiomatic: Nouwanwendun Sizhong

sentences.zh: 耨碗溫敦思忠，本名乙剌補，阿補斯水人。

translations.literal: Nouwanwendun Sizhong, original name Yilabu, was a man of the Apusi River.
translations.idiomatic: Nouwanwendun Sizhong, born Yilabu, came from the Apusi River region.

sentences.zh: 太祖伐遼，是時未有文字，凡軍事當中複而應密者，諸將皆口授思忠，思忠面奏受詔，還軍傳致詔辭，雖往復數千言，無少誤。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor campaigned against Liao, there was as yet no writing; for all military matters requiring secrecy in transmission, the generals orally entrusted them to Sizhong. Sizhong would face the throne to receive the edict, return to the army and transmit the edict's wording; even when the exchange ran to several thousand words, there was not the slightest error.
translations.idiomatic: During Taizu's campaign against Liao, before the state had a written script, every confidential military order passed through the generals' mouths to Sizhong. He received the edict in audience and carried its wording back to the army; even exchanges of thousands of words went without a single mistake.

sentences.zh: 及遼人議和，思忠與烏林答贊謀往來專對其間，號閘剌。

translations.literal: When the Liao sought peace, Sizhong and Wulinada Zanmou went back and forth as sole negotiators between them, and were called zhaci.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao opened peace talks, Sizhong and Wulinada Zanmou served as the sole envoys shuttling between the sides and were called zhaci.

sentences.zh: 閘剌者，漢語雲行人也。

translations.literal: Zhaci, in Chinese, means "traveler."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaci is Chinese for "traveler."

sentences.zh: 自收國元年正月，遼人遣僧家奴來，使者三往反，議不決。

translations.literal: From the first month of the first year of Shouguo the Liao sent the monk Jianu; envoys went back and forth three times, yet the talks could not be settled.
translations.idiomatic: From the first month of Shouguo 1 the Liao sent the monk Jianu; after three rounds of envoys the talks still failed.

sentences.zh: 使者賽剌至遼，遼人殺之。

translations.literal: The envoy Saila reached Liao, and the Liao killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy Saila reached Liao, they killed him.

sentences.zh: 遼主自將，至駝門，大敗，歸，複遣使議和。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler led the army in person, reached Tuomen, suffered a great defeat, returned, and again sent envoys to discuss peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor took the field in person, was routed at Tuomen, withdrew, and again sent envoys to negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 太祖使胡突袞往，書曰：「若不從此，胡突袞但使人送至界上，或如賽剌殺之，惟所欲者。」

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor sent Hutugun with a letter saying: "If you do not accept this, Hutugun need only have men escort you to the border — or kill you as with Saila; do as you please."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Hutugun with a letter: "If you refuse, Hutugun need only have you escorted to the border — or killed like Saila; do as you will."

sentences.zh: 天輔三年六月，遼大冊使太傅習泥烈以冊璽至上京一舍，先取冊文副錄閱視，文不稱兄，不稱大金，稱東懷國。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Tianfu, the Liao grand investiture envoy, Grand Preceptor Xini Lie, brought the investiture documents and seal to within one li of the Supreme Capital. They first took a copy of the text to examine it; the text did not address Jin as elder brother, did not call it Great Jin, but called it the Eastern Huai State.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tianfu 3 the Liao grand investiture envoy, Grand Preceptor Xini Lie, brought the documents and seal to within a li of the Supreme Capital. A copy was read first: it did not treat Jin as elder brother, did not say Great Jin, but called it the Eastern Huai State.

sentences.zh: 太祖不受，使宗翰、宗雄、宗幹、希尹商定冊文義指，揚朴潤色，胡十答、阿撒、高慶裔譯契丹字，使贊謀與習泥烈偕行。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor would not accept it and had Zonghan, Zongxiong, Zonggan, and Xiyin fix the meaning of the investiture text, Yang Pu polish the wording, Hu Shida, Asa, and Gao Qingyi translate the Khitan script, and sent Zanmou to travel with Xini Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu refused it and had Zonghan, Zongxiong, Zonggan, and Xiyin settle the text's meaning, Yang Pu refine the language, Hu Shida, Asa, and Gao Qingyi render the Khitan script, and sent Zanmou back with Xini Lie.

sentences.zh: 贊謀至遼，見遼人再撰冊文，複不盡如本國旨意，欲見遼主自陳，閽者止之。

translations.literal: When Zanmou reached Liao he saw that the Liao had again drafted the investiture text, which still did not fully accord with his state's intent. He wished to see the Liao ruler and state the case himself, but the gatekeepers stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: At Liao, Zanmou found they had drafted a new text that still fell short of Jin's demands. He tried to see the Liao emperor in person, but the gatekeepers barred him.

sentences.zh: 贊謀不顧，直入。

translations.literal: Zanmou paid no heed and went straight in.
translations.idiomatic: Zanmou ignored them and forced his way in.

sentences.zh: 閽者相與搏撠，折其信牌。

translations.literal: The gatekeepers together grappled with him and broke his credential tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeepers seized him and broke his credential tablet.

sentences.zh: 遼人懼，遽遣贊謀歸。

translations.literal: The Liao were afraid and hastily sent Zanmou back.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the Liao hurried him back.

sentences.zh: 太祖再遣贊謀如遼。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor again sent Zanmou to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Zanmou to Liao again.

sentences.zh: 遼人前後十三遣使，和議終不可成。

translations.literal: The Liao sent envoys thirteen times back and forth, yet peace talks could never be concluded.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao sent envoys back and forth thirteen times, but peace could never be made.

sentences.zh: 太祖自將，遂克臨潢。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor led the army in person and then took Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took the field in person and captured Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 其後伐宋，思忠從宗翰軍，封劉豫為齊帝，思忠為傳宣使，俄授謀克。

translations.literal: Later, campaigning against Song, Sizhong followed Zonghan's army; Liu Yu was enfeoffed as Emperor of Qi, and Sizhong was made transmission envoy; shortly afterward he was granted the title of mouke.
translations.idiomatic: In the later campaign against Song he served under Zonghan; when Liu Yu was made Emperor of Qi, Sizhong became transmission envoy and soon received the rank of mouke.

sentences.zh: 從宗弼克和尚原。

translations.literal: He followed Zongbi in taking Heshangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zongbi to victory at Heshangyuan.

sentences.zh: 還為同知西京留守事。

translations.literal: On his return he became associate commissioner of the Western Capital garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was made associate commissioner of the Western Capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 天眷初，改蒲州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjuan he was transferred to defense commissioner of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjuan he was made defense commissioner of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 元帥府在陝西者，其官屬往往豪壓貧民為奴，起遣工匠千人東來，至河上，思忠留止其人以聞，詔皆還之。

translations.literal: Among the marshalate officials in Shaanxi, subordinates often used force to press poor commoners into slavery and raised a thousand artisans to send east. When they reached the river, Sizhong detained them and reported; an edict ordered all to be sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Marshalate officials in Shaanxi often bullied the poor into slavery and drafted a thousand artisans for the east. At the river Sizhong held them and reported; an edict sent them all home.

sentences.zh: 為行台尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He became left vice director of the traveling secretariat's Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left vice director of the traveling secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是時，贊謨為行台參知政事，思忠黷貨無厭，贊謨鄙之，兩人由是交惡。

translations.literal: At this time Zanmo was participating administrator of the traveling secretariat; Sizhong was insatiable in taking bribes, and Zanmo despised him — from this the two became enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Zanmo was then participating administrator of the traveling secretariat. Sizhong's greed for bribes disgusted him, and the two became bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 海陵殺左丞相秉德于行台。

translations.literal: Hailing killed Left Chief Councilor Bingde at the traveling secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing executed Left Chief Councilor Bingde at the traveling secretariat.

sentences.zh: 贊謨妻，秉德乳母也。

translations.literal: Zanmo's wife was Bingde's wet nurse.
translations.idiomatic: Zanmo's wife had been Bingde's wet nurse.

sentences.zh: 思忠因構贊謨。

translations.literal: Sizhong thereupon framed Zanmo.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong then framed Zanmo.

sentences.zh: 殺之。

translations.literal: He was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zanmo was executed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，思忠入為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: That year Sizhong entered the capital as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sizhong came to court as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄進平章政事，封郜國公。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was advanced to chief councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made chief councilor and created Duke of Gao.

sentences.zh: 進拜左丞相兼侍中，封沂國公。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to left chief councilor and concurrently palace attendant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left chief councilor and palace attendant and created Duke of Yi.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiande he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 3 he retired.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年十月，海陵率三品以上官幸思忠第，使以家禮見，謂思忠曰：「卿神氣康實，習先朝舊事，舍卿無能知者，當為朕起，共治國政。」

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Zhenyuan, Hailing led officials of the third rank and above to visit Sizhong's residence, had him received with family ceremony, and said to Sizhong: "Your spirit is vigorous and sound; you are versed in the affairs of the former court. Apart from you there is no one who knows them. You must rise for me and together govern the state."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Zhenyuan 2, Hailing led third-rank officials and above to Sizhong's home and received him with family rites. He told Sizhong: "You are hale and know the old court's ways as no one else does. Rise and govern with me."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「君之命，臣敢不敬從，但恨老病疏謬，無以塞責耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "A lord's command — how dare a minister not respectfully obey? I only regret that old age and illness make me negligent and confused, so that I cannot fulfill the charge."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Your command I dare not refuse, but age and illness leave me unfit for the task."

sentences.zh: 遂命思忠乘馬從入宮，拜太傅，領三省事，封齊國王。

translations.literal: He then ordered Sizhong to mount and follow him into the palace, appointed him Grand Preceptor, put him in charge of the Three Departments, and enfeoffed him as King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He had Sizhong ride with him into the palace, made him Grand Preceptor in charge of the Three Departments, and created him King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 尋拜太師兼勸農使。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Grand Tutor and concurrently commissioner for encouraging agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Grand Tutor and commissioner for encouraging agriculture.

sentences.zh: 已而罷中書門下省，不置領三省事。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the Secretariat-Chancellery was abolished and the post of overseer of the Three Departments was not re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Secretariat-Chancellery was abolished and the post overseeing the Three Departments was dropped.

sentences.zh: 置尚書令，位丞相上。

translations.literal: The office of Director of the Department of State Affairs was established, ranking above the chief councilors.
translations.idiomatic: The office of Director of the Department of State Affairs was created, ranking above the chief councilors.

sentences.zh: 思忠為尚書令，特置散從八人，聽隨至宮，省奏賜坐。

translations.literal: Sizhong became Director; eight personal attendants were specially appointed, permitted to follow him to the palace, where memorials were read and he was granted a seat.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong became Director, with eight personal attendants allowed to accompany him to court, where memorials were read and he was given a seat.

sentences.zh: 海陵欲定封爵制度，風思忠建白之。

translations.literal: Hailing wished to fix the system of enfeoffment and titles and prompted Sizhong to propose it.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing wanted to reform enfeoffments and prompted Sizhong to draft the proposal.

sentences.zh: 封王者皆降封，異姓或封公或一品、二品階。

translations.literal: All who had been enfeoffed as kings were reduced in rank; those of other surnames were enfeoffed as dukes or given first- or second-rank grades.
translations.idiomatic: Former kings were demoted; men of other surnames received dukedoms or first- or second-rank grades.

sentences.zh: 惟封思忠廣平郡王，賜以玉帶。

translations.literal: Only Sizhong was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping Commandery and given an imperial jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: Only Sizhong was created Prince of Guangping and given an imperial jade belt.

sentences.zh: 思忠言百官不當封妻，海陵從之。

translations.literal: Sizhong said that officials should not enfeoff their wives; Hailing followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong argued that officials should not enfeoff their wives, and Hailing agreed.

sentences.zh: 惟封思忠次室為郡夫人。

translations.literal: Only Sizhong's secondary consort was enfeoffed as Lady of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Only his secondary consort was created Lady of the Commandery.

sentences.zh: 而思忠亦自謂太祖舊臣，頗自任，雖海陵遂非拒諫，而思忠盡言無所避。

translations.literal: Sizhong also considered himself an old servant of Taizu and took considerable liberty; though Hailing persisted in error and rejected remonstrance, Sizhong spoke his mind without avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong counted himself an old servant of Taizu and spoke freely; even when Hailing grew stubborn and rejected counsel, he held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 海陵將伐宋，問諸大臣，皆不敢對。

translations.literal: When Hailing was about to campaign against Song, he questioned the chief ministers; none dared answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing planned war on Song, he asked his ministers; none dared reply.

sentences.zh: 思忠曰：「不可。」

translations.literal: Sizhong said: "It cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong said: "You must not."

sentences.zh: 海陵不悅，謂思忠曰：「汝勿論可否，但雲何時克之。」

translations.literal: Hailing was displeased and told Sizhong: "Do not discuss whether it can be done — only say when it will be conquered."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was angry. "Never mind whether it can be done," he said. "Tell me when you will conquer it."

sentences.zh: 思忠曰：「以十年為期。」

translations.literal: Sizhong said: "Set a term of ten years."
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong said: "Give it ten years."

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「何久也？

translations.literal: Hailing said: "Why so long?
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said: "Why so long?

sentences.zh: 期月耳。」

translations.literal: A month will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: A month will do."

sentences.zh: 思忠曰：「太祖伐遼，猶且數年。

translations.literal: Sizhong said: "When Taizu campaigned against Liao, it still took several years.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong said: "Taizu's conquest of Liao took years.

sentences.zh: 今百姓愁怨，師出無名。

translations.literal: Now the common people are full of grief and resentment; to send the army forth has no proper name.
translations.idiomatic: The people are bitter, and this war has no just cause.

sentences.zh: 江、淮間暑熱湫濕，不堪久居，未能以歲月期也。」

translations.literal: Between the Yangzi and Huai the heat is oppressive and the air close and damp — one cannot long remain there; it cannot be set by months."
translations.idiomatic: Between the Yangzi and Huai the heat and damp are unbearable for long campaigns; you cannot reckon it by months."

sentences.zh: 海陵怒，顧視左右，若欲取兵刃者。

translations.literal: Hailing was furious and looked about him as if to seize a weapon.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing glared about as if to reach for a weapon.

sentences.zh: 思忠無所畏恐，複曰：「老臣曆事四朝，位至公相，苟有補於國家，死亦何憾。」

translations.literal: Sizhong showed no fear and said again: "This old minister has served four reigns and risen to duke and chief councilor; if there is any benefit to the state, what regret is there in death?"
translations.idiomatic: Unafraid, Sizhong said again: "I have served four reigns and risen to the highest rank; if my words help the state, I die without regret."

sentences.zh: 有頃，海陵曰：「自古帝王混一天下，然後可為正統。

translations.literal: After a moment Hailing said: "From antiquity emperors have unified all under Heaven and only then could be called orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: After a pause Hailing said: "Since antiquity only emperors who unified the realm could claim orthodox rule.

sentences.zh: 爾耄夫固不知此，汝子乙迭讀書，可往問之。」

translations.literal: You old man surely do not know this; your son Yidie studies books — you may go ask him."
translations.idiomatic: You old fool cannot grasp this; your son Yidie reads books — go ask him."

sentences.zh: 思忠曰：「臣昔見太祖取天下，此時豈有文字耶？

translations.literal: Sizhong said: "When I formerly saw Taizu take the realm under Heaven, was there writing then?
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong said: "When I watched Taizu win the empire, was there any writing then?

sentences.zh: 臣年垂七十，更事多矣，彼乳臭子，安足問哉！」

translations.literal: I am nearly seventy and have seen much; what is that milk-smelling boy worth asking?"
translations.idiomatic: I am nearly seventy and have seen much; what can that suckling child tell me?"

sentences.zh: 海陵既不用思忠言，運四方甲仗於中都。

translations.literal: Hailing, having not taken Sizhong's advice, transported armor and weapons from the four directions to the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ignoring Sizhong, Hailing gathered arms from every quarter to the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 思忠曰：「州郡無兵，何以備盜賊？」

translations.literal: Sizhong said: "If the prefectures and commanderies have no troops, how will they guard against bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong said: "Without local troops, how will the provinces check bandits?"

sentences.zh: 海陵盡籍丁壯為兵，思忠曰：「山后契丹諸部，恐未可盡起。」

translations.literal: Hailing registered all able-bodied men as soldiers. Sizhong said: "The Khitan tribes beyond the mountains — I fear they cannot all be mobilized."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing conscripted every able man. Sizhong warned: "The Khitan tribes beyond the mountains may not all be safe to mobilize."

sentences.zh: 皆不聽。

translations.literal: He listened to none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing would not listen.

sentences.zh: 其後，州郡盜起，守令不能制。

translations.literal: Afterward bandits rose in the prefectures and commanderies, and the prefects and magistrates could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry soon spread through the provinces, beyond the control of local officials.

sentences.zh: 契丹撒八、窩斡果反，期年乃克之。

translations.literal: The Khitan Sab'a and Wowo did in fact rebel, and it took a full year to subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan Sab'a and Wowo rebelled, and a full year passed before they were suppressed.

sentences.zh: 子 謙

translations.literal: Son: Qian
translations.idiomatic: Son: Qian

sentences.zh: 謙，本名乙迭，累官禦史中丞。

translations.literal: Qian, original name Yidie, rose through offices to censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, born Yidie, rose to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 世宗謂之曰：「省部官受請托，有以室家傳達者。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor told him: "Department officials accept bribes, and some use their households to convey them.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizong Emperor told him: "Department officials take bribes, and some pass them through their households.

sentences.zh: 官刑不肅，士風頹弊如此，其糾正之。」

translations.literal: Official discipline is not strict and the moral tone of scholars has decayed to this point — correct it."
translations.idiomatic: Discipline is lax and official morals have sunk this low — set it right."

sentences.zh: 初，世宗至中都，多放宮人還家，有稱心等數人在放遣之例，所司失於檢照，不得出宮，心常怏怏。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Shizong Emperor reached the Central Capital, many palace women were released to return home. Several including Chengxin were on the release list, but the responsible office failed in its review and they could not leave the palace; they were always resentful at heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong first reached the Central Capital, many palace women were sent home. Chengxin and several others were on the release list, but a clerical error kept them inside, and they brooded over the wrong.

sentences.zh: 大定二年閏二月癸巳夜，遂於十六位放火，延燒太和、神龍殿。

translations.literal: On the night of guisi, intercalary second month of the second year of Dadu, they set fire in the Sixteen Quarters, which spread to burn the Taihe and Shenlong halls.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of guisi in the intercalary second month of Dadu 2 they set fire in the Sixteen Quarters, and the blaze spread to the Taihe and Shenlong halls.

sentences.zh: 上命近臣跡火之所發。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered close attendants to trace where the fire had started.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his attendants to trace the fire's origin.

sentences.zh: 十六位宮人袁六娘等六人告，實稱心等為之。

translations.literal: Six palace women of the Sixteen Quarters, Yuan Liuniang and five others, reported that in fact Chengxin and the others had done it.
translations.idiomatic: Six palace women of the Sixteen Quarters, led by Yuan Liuniang, reported that Chengxin and her companions had set the fire.

sentences.zh: 稱心等伏誅，賞賜袁六娘六人，放出宮為良。

translations.literal: Chengxin and the others were executed; Yuan Liuniang and the six were rewarded and released from the palace as free commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxin and her accomplices were executed; Yuan Liuniang and the other five were rewarded and freed from palace service.

sentences.zh: 謙意宮殿被火，將復興工役，勞民傷財，乃上表乞權紓修建。

translations.literal: Qian feared that with the palace halls burned, reconstruction labor would be revived, taxing the people and wasting wealth; he therefore submitted a memorial asking to defer rebuilding for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that the fire would trigger costly rebuilding that would burden the people, Qian memorialized to defer construction.

sentences.zh: 上使張汝弼詔謙曰：「朕思正隆比年徭役，百姓瘡痍未複，邊事未息，豈遽有營繕也。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Zhang Rubi with an edict to Qian, saying: "I reflect that in the Zhenglong years corvée was heavy year after year; the common people's wounds are not yet healed, and border affairs have not ceased — how could we hastily undertake construction?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zhang Rubi to tell Qian: "I know the Zhenglong years exhausted the people; their wounds are not healed and the borders are still troubled — how could I rush into rebuilding?

sentences.zh: 卿可悉之。」

translations.literal: You may understand this fully."
translations.idiomatic: You may take that as settled."

sentences.zh: 久之，襲父思忠濟州猛安、利涉軍節度副使。

translations.literal: After a long time he inherited his father Sizhong's post as meng'an of Jizhou and deputy military commissioner of the Lishé Army.
translations.idiomatic: In time he inherited his father Sizhong's meng'an of Jizhou and deputy command of the Lishé Army.

sentences.zh: 烏林答鈔兀追捕逃軍，至猛安中，謙畏其擾，乃醵民財買銀賂鈔兀。

translations.literal: Wulinada Chaowu pursued deserters into the meng'an district; Qian feared his harassment and therefore pooled commoners' wealth to buy silver and bribe Chaowu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wulinada Chaowu came hunting deserters in the meng'an, Qian, fearing harassment, levied silver from the people to bribe him.

sentences.zh: 事覺，鈔兀抵罪，謙坐奪猛安。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light, Chaowu was punished by law and Qian was deprived of his meng'an on the charge.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was exposed, Chaowu was punished and Qian lost his meng'an.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，求敘。

translations.literal: When an amnesty was declared, he sought restoration.
translations.idiomatic: After an amnesty he sought restoration.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「乙迭無自與贓，使複其所。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yidie did not take the bribe himself; let him be restored to his post."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Yidie did not take the bribe himself; restore his post."

sentences.zh: 侄 兀帶

translations.literal: Nephew: Wudai
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Wudai

sentences.zh: 耨碗溫敦兀帶，太師思忠侄也。

translations.literal: Nouwanwendun Wudai was the nephew of Grand Tutor Sizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Nouwanwendun Wudai was the nephew of Grand Tutor Sizhong.

sentences.zh: 天會間，充女直字學生，學問通達，觀書史，工為詩。

translations.literal: During Tianhui he served as a Jurchen-script student; his learning was thorough, he read histories, and he was skilled at composing poetry.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianhui he studied Jurchen script; widely learned, he read histories and wrote poetry well.

sentences.zh: 選為尚書省令史，除右司都事，轉行台右司郎中，入為左司員外郎。

translations.literal: He was selected as a clerk of the Department of State Affairs, appointed director of the right bureau, transferred to traveling secretariat right bureau director, and entered the capital as outer vice director of the left bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Department of State Affairs clerk, then director of the right bureau, traveling secretariat right bureau director, and outer vice director of the left bureau at court.

sentences.zh: 累官同知大興尹，京師盜賊止息，事無留滯。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he became associate prefect of Daxing; banditry in the capital ceased and no business was left pending.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to associate prefect of Daxing; capital crime stopped and no case lingered on his desk.

sentences.zh: 再遷刑部尚書，改定海軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Minister of Justice and then made military commissioner of the Dinghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Justice, then military commissioner of the Dinghai Army.

sentences.zh: 除兵部尚書，改吏部。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of War and then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of War, then Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 正隆伐宋。

translations.literal: During the Zhenglong campaign against Song —
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenglong campaign against Song —

sentences.zh: 為武定軍都總管。

translations.literal: he became overall commander of the Wuding Army.
translations.idiomatic: he was overall commander of the Wuding Army.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，遣使召之，授咸平尹，為北邊行軍都統。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor took the throne, he sent envoys to summon him, appointed him prefect of Xianping, and made him overall commander of the northern frontier army.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne he summoned Wudai, made him prefect of Xianping, and overall commander on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 改會甯尹，都統如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Huining while retaining his command as overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Huining as prefect while keeping his frontier command.

sentences.zh: 是時初定窩斡，人心未安，兀帶為治寬簡，多備禦，謹斥候，邊郡以寧。

translations.literal: At this time Wowo's rebellion had just been settled and hearts were not yet at ease; Wudai governed with leniency and simplicity, made many defensive preparations, and kept scouts strict — the border commanderies were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: With Wowo's rebellion just suppressed and the frontier still uneasy, Wudai ruled lightly but fortified the border and kept scouts alert, and the frontier counties grew calm.

sentences.zh: 改北京留守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to commissioner of the Northern Capital garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commissioner of the Northern Capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 以廉察舉「兀帶所在有能名，無私過」，由是入拜參知政事。

translations.literal: On integrity inspection he was cited as "wherever Wudai has been, he has a reputation for ability and no private faults," and on this basis he entered court as participating administrator of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: An integrity review praised him as capable and without private fault wherever he had served, and he was made participating administrator of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 世宗諭之曰：「凡在卿上者，行事或不當理，咨稟不從，卿以所見奏聞。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor instructed him: "Whenever those above you act contrary to reason and will not heed consultation, report what you see to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong told him: "If your superiors act wrongly and ignore your advice, report what you see directly to me.

sentences.zh: 下位有可用之才，當推薦之。」

translations.literal: When subordinates have talent that can be used, you should recommend them."
translations.idiomatic: When you find able men below you, recommend them."

sentences.zh: 久之，屬疾，上命左宣徽使敬嗣暉往視，遣醫治療。

translations.literal: After a long time he fell ill; the emperor ordered Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Jing Sihui to visit him and sent physicians to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: In time he fell ill; the emperor sent Left Commissioner Jing Sihui to visit him and physicians to treat him.

sentences.zh: 薨，年四十七。

translations.literal: He died; he was forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 上聞悼惜之，賻銀千兩、重彩四十端、絹四百匹，敕有司致祭。

translations.literal: On hearing, the emperor mourned and regretted it, bestowing one thousand taels of silver, forty bolts of heavy brocade, and four hundred bolts of silk, and ordering the responsible offices to perform sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him and sent one thousand taels of silver, forty bolts of brocade, four hundred bolts of silk, and ordered the rites office to perform sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 久之，上謂侍臣曰：「故參知政事兀帶、刑部尚書彥忠、滄州節度使兀不喝、侍郎敵斡、郎中骨赧皆為人忠直，後進中少有能及之者。

translations.literal: After a long time the emperor told his attendants: "The late participating administrator Wudai, Minister of Justice Yanzhong, military commissioner of Cangzhou Wubuhai, vice director of the Secretariat Diwo, and bureau director Guhan were all upright men; among the younger generation few can equal them.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward the emperor told his attendants: "The late Wudai, Yanzhong, Wubuhai, Diwo, and Guhan were all upright; few of the younger men measure up to them.

sentences.zh: 朕樂得忠直之人，有如兀帶輩者乎，卿等為朕舉之。」

translations.literal: I delight in obtaining upright men — are there any like Wudai and his kind? You should recommend them to me."
translations.idiomatic: I want upright men like Wudai — find them for me."

sentences.zh: 其見思如此。

translations.literal: Such was the regard in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 昂，本名奔睹，景祖弟孛黑之孫，斜斡之子。

translations.literal: Ang, original name Bendu, was grandson of Jingzu's younger brother Lihei and son of Xie'o.
translations.idiomatic: Ang, born Bendu, was the grandson of Jingzu's brother Lihei and the son of Xie'o.

sentences.zh: 幼時侍太祖。

translations.literal: In youth he attended the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he attended Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖令數人兩兩角力。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor had several men wrestle in pairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had several men wrestle in pairs.

sentences.zh: 時昂年十五，太祖顧曰：「汝能此乎？」

translations.literal: Ang was then fifteen; the Taizu Emperor looked at him and said: "Can you do this?"
translations.idiomatic: Ang was fifteen. Taizu turned to him and asked: "Can you do this?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「有命，敢不勉。」

translations.literal: He replied: "If there is a command, how dare I not strive?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "If you command it, I shall try."

sentences.zh: 遂連僕六人。

translations.literal: He thereupon threw six men in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He threw six men in a row.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜曰：「汝，吾宗弟也，自今勿遠左右。」

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor was pleased and said: "You are a clansman of mine; from now on do not stray far from my side."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was delighted. "You are kin of my house," he said; "stay close to me from now on."

sentences.zh: 居數日，賜金牌，令佩以侍。

translations.literal: After several days he bestowed a gold tablet and ordered him to wear it while attending.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he gave him a gold tablet and had him wear it in attendance.

sentences.zh: 年十七，太祖伐遼，謂之曰：「汝可擐甲從軍矣。」

translations.literal: At seventeen, when the Taizu Emperor campaigned against Liao, he told him: "You may don armor and follow the army."
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, when Taizu marched against Liao, he told him: "You are old enough to take the field."

sentences.zh: 昂遂佩所賜金牌從軍。

translations.literal: Ang thereupon wore the gold tablet he had been given and followed the army.
translations.idiomatic: Ang wore the gold tablet he had been given and joined the campaign.

sentences.zh: 太祖平燕，策功，賜甲第一區。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor pacified Yan, his merit was assessed and he was given one first-grade suit of armor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu pacified Yan, Ang was rewarded with a first-grade suit of armor for his service.

sentences.zh: 天輔六年，宗翰駐北安州，聞遼主延禧在鴛鴦濼，遣耨碗溫敦思忠請于國論勃極烈杲，願以所部軍追之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu, Zonghan was stationed at Beian Prefecture. Hearing that the Liao ruler Yelü Yanxi was at Yuanyang Marsh, he sent Nouwanwendun Sizhong to request of Gao, the delian of the national council, permission to pursue him with the troops under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu, Zonghan held Beian Prefecture. Learning that the Liao emperor Yelü Yanxi was at Yuanyang Marsh, he dispatched Nouwanwendun Sizhong to ask Gao, chief delian of the national council, for leave to pursue with his own forces.

sentences.zh: 杲不能決，乃遣昂與思忠詣宗翰議，其事遂定。

translations.literal: Gao could not decide, so he sent Ang and Sizhong to go to Zonghan to discuss it, and the matter was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Gao could not decide alone, so he sent Ang and Sizhong to confer with Zonghan; the plan was then fixed.

sentences.zh: 天會二年，南京叛，軍帥闍母遣昂、劉彥宗分兵討之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhui, the Southern Capital rebelled. The army commander Zhanmu dispatched Ang and Liu Yanzong with divided forces to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhui, the Southern Capital rose in revolt. The army commander Zhanmu sent Ang and Liu Yanzong with separate columns to put it down.

sentences.zh: 宗望伐宋，承制以為河南諸路兵馬都統，稱「金牌郎君」。

translations.literal: When Zongwang invaded Song, by provisional order Ang was made overall commander of the armies and horses of the various Henan circuits, styled "Golden Tablet Lord."
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang marched against Song, Ang was provisionally appointed overall commander of Henan circuit forces and styled "Lord of the Golden Tablet."

sentences.zh: 及攻汴州，宗弼與昂以兵三千為前鋒。

translations.literal: When they attacked Bianzhou, Zongbi and Ang served as vanguard with three thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Bianzhou, Zongbi and Ang led three thousand men as the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 比暮，昂先以兵千人馳至其北門。

translations.literal: By evening, Ang had first raced with a thousand troops to its north gate.
translations.idiomatic: By dusk Ang had galloped ahead with a thousand men to the north gate.

sentences.zh: 時軍中遣使入城，宋人不納。

translations.literal: At that time the army sent envoys into the city, but the Song would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: The army sent envoys into the city, but the Song refused them entry.

sentences.zh: 昂諭之以事，遂得入。

translations.literal: Ang explained the matter to them, and entry was then obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Ang explained matters to the defenders, and they were admitted.

sentences.zh: 宗望至汴，令闍母、撻懶等屯于城之東北隅。

translations.literal: When Zongwang reached Bian, he ordered Zhanmu, Talan, and others to encamp at the northeast corner of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang reached Bianjing, he stationed Zhanmu, Talan, and others at the city's northeast corner.

sentences.zh: 慮宋主遁去，遣昂等率輕騎環城巡邏。

translations.literal: Fearing the Song emperor would slip away, he dispatched Ang and others to lead light cavalry to patrol around the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Song emperor might escape, he sent Ang and others with light cavalry to circle the walls on patrol.

sentences.zh: 昂所領止八謀克，遇敵萬人，與戰，敗之，其步軍溺死於汴者過半。

translations.literal: Ang commanded only eight meng'an units. He encountered ten thousand enemies, joined battle, and defeated them; more than half of their infantry drowned in the Bian River.
translations.idiomatic: Ang had only eight meng'an companies. He met ten thousand enemy troops, fought them, and routed them—more than half the Song infantry drowned in the Bian River.

sentences.zh: 七年，大軍渡江，敗宋兵于江上。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the great army crossed the river and defeated Song troops on the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the main army crossed the Yangzi and defeated Song forces on the river.

sentences.zh: 帥府遣昂等以兵追宋主。

translations.literal: The marshal's headquarters dispatched Ang and others with troops to pursue the Song emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The command post sent Ang and others in pursuit of the Song emperor.

sentences.zh: 宋主入會稽，若為堅守計，有兵數千列陣于郭東竹葦間。

translations.literal: The Song emperor entered Kuaiji. As if planning a stubborn defense, several thousand troops were drawn up in formation among the reeds east of the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor withdrew into Kuaiji. As though preparing to hold firm, several thousand soldiers were arrayed among the bamboo and reeds east of the suburb.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲擊之，昂曰：「此詐也。

translations.literal: The generals wished to attack them. Ang said: "This is a ruse.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to strike, but Ang said, "This is a feint.

sentences.zh: 不若急攻城，不然將由他門逸去。」

translations.literal: Better to press the assault on the city at once; otherwise he will escape through another gate."
translations.idiomatic: Better to storm the city at once—or he will slip out through another gate."

sentences.zh: 諸將猶豫未決，而宋主果於他門以單舟入海，不獲而還。

translations.literal: The generals hesitated and could not decide. The Song emperor indeed took a single boat through another gate and put out to sea; they failed to capture him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wavered and could not decide. The Song emperor did escape by a single boat through another gate and put to sea; they returned empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 宗輔定陝西，宗弼經略熙秦，遣昂與撒離喝領兵八千攻取河西郡縣。

translations.literal: Zongfu pacified Shaanxi; Zongbi administered Xihé and Qin. He dispatched Ang and Saliha to lead eight thousand troops to seize the commanderies and counties of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongfu secured Shaanxi, Zongbi took charge of Xihé and Qin and sent Ang and Saliha with eight thousand men to take the Hexi prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 昂等遂取甯洮、安隴二寨。

translations.literal: Ang and the others then took the two stockades of Ningtao and Anlong.
translations.idiomatic: Ang and his forces took the Ningtao and Anlong stockades.

sentences.zh: 進至河州，其通判率士民迎降。

translations.literal: Advancing to Hezhou, its vice prefect led officials and people to welcome and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced to Hezhou, where the vice prefect led officials and townspeople out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 攻樂州，其都護及河州安撫使郭寧偕降。

translations.literal: They attacked Lezhou; its protector and Hezhou pacification commissioner Guo Ning surrendered together.
translations.idiomatic: At Lezhou the protector and Hezhou pacification commissioner Guo Ning surrendered together.

sentences.zh: 複進取三寨，至西寧州，都護許居簡以城降，吐蕃酋長之孫趙鈐轄率其所部木波首領五人來降。

translations.literal: They again advanced and took three stockades. Reaching Xining Prefecture, Protector Xu Jujian surrendered the city. Zhao Qianxia, grandson of a Tibetan chieftain, led five Mubo chieftains of his command to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They took three more stockades and reached Xining, where Protector Xu Jujian handed over the city. Zhao Qianxia, grandson of a Tibetan chieftain, brought five Mubo chieftains under his command to submit.

sentences.zh: 昂別領軍四千往積石軍，降其軍及所部五寨官吏。

translations.literal: Ang separately led four thousand troops to Jishi Army and received the surrender of that army and the officials of five stockades under its command.
translations.idiomatic: Ang detached four thousand men for Jishi Army and accepted the surrender of the garrison and the officials of five dependent stockades.

sentences.zh: 追吐蕃鈐轄等十二人至廓州，招之不下，攻取之。

translations.literal: Pursuing twelve Tibetan qianxia and others to Kuozhou, he summoned them to submit but they would not; he attacked and took the place.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued twelve Tibetan commanders as far as Kuozhou. When they refused to submit, he stormed the city and took it.

sentences.zh: 天眷元年，授鎮國上將軍，除東平尹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjuan he was granted General Who Stabilizes the State and appointed Administrator of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjuan he was made General Who Stabilizes the State and appointed Administrator of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，宋將岳飛以兵十萬，號稱百萬，來攻東平。

translations.literal: The next summer, the Song general Yue Fei came with a hundred thousand troops, proclaiming a million, to attack Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: The next summer the Song general Yue Fei marched on Dongping with a hundred thousand men, claiming a million.

sentences.zh: 東平有兵五千，倉卒出禦之。

translations.literal: Dongping had only five thousand troops; they sallied out in haste to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Dongping had only five thousand troops, which were hurriedly sent out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 時桑柘方茂，昂使多張旗幟于林間，以為疑兵，自以精兵陣於前。

translations.literal: The mulberry trees were then in full leaf. Ang had many banners displayed in the groves as decoy troops and himself drew up elite troops in the fore.
translations.idiomatic: With the mulberry groves in full leaf, Ang posted many banners among the trees as a feint and drew up his elite troops in front.

sentences.zh: 飛不敢動，相持數日而退。

translations.literal: Yue Fei dared not move; after several days of stalemate he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei held back; after several days he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 昂勒兵襲之，至清口，飛眾泛舟逆水而去。

translations.literal: Ang drove his troops to strike at him. Reaching Qingkou, he found Yue Fei's force going upstream by boat.
translations.idiomatic: Ang pressed the attack as far as Qingkou, where Yue Fei's men were rowing upstream against the current.

sentences.zh: 時霖雨晝夜不止，昂乃附水屯營。

translations.literal: At that time torrential rain fell day and night without cease. Ang thereupon encamped close to the water.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night the rains poured; Ang made camp beside the river.

sentences.zh: 夜將半，忽促眾北行。

translations.literal: When the night was nearly half spent, he suddenly urged the host northward.
translations.idiomatic: Near midnight he suddenly ordered a march north.

sentences.zh: 諸將諫曰：「軍士遠涉泥淖，饑憊未食，恐難遽行。」

translations.literal: The generals remonstrated, saying: "The soldiers have struggled far through mud and mire; hungry and weary, they have not eaten—it will be hard to move at once."
translations.idiomatic: The generals protested: "The men have slogged through mud for miles—they are hungry, exhausted, and unfed. A sudden march will be impossible."

sentences.zh: 昂怒不應，鳴鼓督之，下令曰：「鼓聲絕而敢後者斬。」

translations.literal: Ang angrily gave no reply. He sounded the drums to press them on and issued an order: "When the drumbeats cease, whoever dares lag behind shall be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Ang ignored them in anger, beat the drums, and ordered: "When the drums fall silent, any man who hangs back is beheaded."

sentences.zh: 遂棄營去，幾二十里而止。

translations.literal: They thereupon abandoned the camp and left, halting after nearly twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: They abandoned camp and marched nearly twenty li before halting.

sentences.zh: 是夜，宋人來劫營，無所得而去。

translations.literal: That night Song men came to raid the camp but gained nothing and departed.
translations.idiomatic: That night Song raiders struck the abandoned camp and returned empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 諸將入賀，且問其故。

translations.literal: The generals entered to congratulate him and also asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The generals came to congratulate him and ask what he had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 昂曰：「沿流而下者，走也；

translations.literal: Ang said: "Those going downstream are fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: Ang said, "Moving downstream is flight.

sentences.zh: 溯流而上者，誘我必追也。

translations.literal: Those going upstream are luring us to chase them.
translations.idiomatic: Moving upstream is bait—they mean to draw us into pursuit.

sentences.zh: 今大雨泥淖，彼舟行安，我陸行勞。

translations.literal: Now with heavy rain and mud, they travel safely by boat while we toil by land.
translations.idiomatic: In this downpour and mud, boats ride easily while we march on land.

sentences.zh: 士卒饑乏，弓矢敗弱，我軍居其下流，勢不便利，其襲我必矣。」

translations.literal: Our soldiers are hungry and spent; bows and arrows are damaged and weak. Our army is below them on the stream—the position is unfavorable—they are sure to raid us."
translations.idiomatic: Our men are hungry, our bows sodden—we hold the lower reach of the river. They were bound to strike us in the night."

sentences.zh: 眾皆稱善。

translations.literal: All praised his judgment.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed he had read the situation aright.

sentences.zh: 岳飛以兵十萬圍邳州甚急，城中兵才千餘，守將懼，遣人求救。

translations.literal: Yue Fei with a hundred thousand troops besieged Pizhou very closely. The city had barely more than a thousand troops. The defending general was afraid and sent someone to beg for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei tightened his siege of Pizhou with a hundred thousand men. The garrison numbered barely a thousand; the commander in terror sent for help.

sentences.zh: 昂曰：「為我語守將，我嘗至下邳，城中西南隅有塹深丈餘，可速實之。」

translations.literal: Ang said: "Tell the defending general for me: I once went to Xiapi. In the southwest corner of the city there is a trench more than a zhang deep—have it filled at once."
translations.idiomatic: Ang said, "Tell the commander: when I was at Xiapi I noticed a trench more than a zhang deep in the southwest corner—fill it at once."

sentences.zh: 守將如其教，填之。

translations.literal: The defending general followed his instruction and filled it in.
translations.idiomatic: The commander did as he was told and filled it in.

sentences.zh: 岳飛果自此穴地以入，知有備，遂止。

translations.literal: Yue Fei indeed intended to tunnel in from there; learning of the preparations, he thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei had indeed planned to mine in there; finding it blocked, he broke off the attempt.

sentences.zh: 昂舉兵以為聲援，飛乃退。

translations.literal: Ang raised troops as a supporting force, and Yue Fei then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ang marched in relief; Yue Fei then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 在東平七年，改益都尹，遷東北路招討使，改崇義軍節度使，遷會寧牧。

translations.literal: After seven years at Dongping, he was transferred to Administrator of Yidu, then promoted to Pacification Commissioner of the Northeast Route, changed to Military Commissioner of the Chongyi Army, and moved to Pastoral Lord of Huining.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years at Dongping he became Administrator of Yidu, then Northeast Route Pacification Commissioner, Military Commissioner of the Chongyi Army, and finally Pastoral Lord of Huining.

sentences.zh: 天德初，改安武軍節度使，遷元帥右都監，轉左監軍，授上京路移裏閔斡魯渾河世襲猛安。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he was changed to Military Commissioner of the Anwu Army, promoted to Right Overseer of the marshal's command, transferred to Left Army Supervisor, and granted the hereditary meng'an of Yili Min Walu Hunhe on the Shangjing Route.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tiande he was made Military Commissioner of the Anwu Army, then Right Overseer under the marshal, then Left Army Supervisor, and granted the hereditary meng'an of Yili Min Walu Hunhe on the Shangjing circuit.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「汝有大功，一猛安不足酬也。」

translations.literal: Hailing said: "You have great merit; one meng'an is not enough to reward you."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "Your service has been great—a single meng'an is too small a reward."

sentences.zh: 益以四謀克。

translations.literal: Four meng'an companies were added.
translations.idiomatic: He added four meng'an companies to the grant.

sentences.zh: 昂受親管謀克，餘三謀克讓其族兄弟。

translations.literal: Ang accepted the personally supervised meng'an and yielded the other three meng'an to his clansmen and brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Ang kept the meng'an under his direct command and gave the other three to kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 拜樞密副使，轉太子少保，進樞密使、尚書左丞相。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and advanced to Commissioner of the Privy Council and Left Grand Councilor of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, then Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then Privy Council Commissioner and Left Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 昂怒族弟妻，去衣杖其脊，海陵聞之，杖昂五十。

translations.literal: Ang, angry at his clansman's wife, stripped her and beat her back with a staff. When Hailing heard of it, he had Ang beaten fifty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: In a rage at a kinsman's wife, Ang had her stripped and beaten. Hailing heard of it and had Ang flogged fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜太尉，封沈國公。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Duke of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was made Grand Commandant and enfeoffed Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 進太保，判大宗正事，封楚國公，累進封莒、衛、齊，兼樞密使，太保如故。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Guardian, assigned to oversee the Office of the Imperial Clan, enfeoffed as Duke of Chu, and repeatedly promoted in rank to Ju, Wei, and Qi while retaining Grand Guardian and concurrently serving as Privy Council Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Guardian and chief of the Imperial Clan Office, was enfeoffed Duke of Chu, and was promoted through the dukedoms of Ju, Wei, and Qi while retaining Grand Guardian and the post of Privy Council Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 海陵南伐，分諸路軍為三十二總管，分隸左右領軍大都督府，遂以昂為左領軍大都督。

translations.literal: When Hailing marched south, the armies of the various routes were divided into thirty-two overall commanders subordinated to the Left and Right Offices of the Leading Army Grand Command; Ang was thereby made Grand Commander of the Left Leading Army.
translations.idiomatic: On Hailing's southern campaign the route armies were organized into thirty-two overall commands under the Left and Right Leading Army Grand Headquarters; Ang was made Grand Commander of the Left.

sentences.zh: 海陵築台于江上，召昂及右領軍副大都督蒲盧渾謂之曰：「舟楫已具，可以濟矣。」

translations.literal: Hailing built a platform on the river and summoned Ang and Puluhun, Deputy Grand Commander of the Right Leading Army, saying: "Boats and oars are ready—we can cross."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing built a platform on the river and summoned Ang and Puluhun, deputy grand commander of the right leading army. "The fleet is ready," he said. "We can cross."

sentences.zh: 蒲盧渾曰：「舟小不可濟。」

translations.literal: Puluhun said: "The boats are too small to cross."
translations.idiomatic: Puluhun replied, "The boats are too small to cross."

sentences.zh: 海陵怒，詔昂與蒲盧渾明日先濟。

translations.literal: Hailing was angered and ordered Ang and Puluhun to cross first the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing flew into a rage and ordered Ang and Puluhun to cross first the next day.

sentences.zh: 昂懼，欲亡去。

translations.literal: Ang was afraid and wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Ang was terrified and thought of fleeing.

sentences.zh: 抵暮，海陵遣人止之曰：「前言一時之怒耳。」

translations.literal: Near evening Hailing sent someone to stop him, saying: "What I said before was only a moment's anger."
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Hailing sent word to stay him: "That was only a passing fit of anger."

sentences.zh: 既而至揚州，軍變，海陵死。

translations.literal: Soon after they reached Yangzhou, the army mutinied and Hailing was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Yangzhou the army mutinied and Hailing was killed.

sentences.zh: 昂在海陵時，縱飲沉酣，輒數日不醒。

translations.literal: While at Hailing's court, Ang drank freely and deeply, often not sobering for several days.
translations.idiomatic: At Hailing's court Ang drank deeply for days on end.

sentences.zh: 海陵聞之，常面戒不令飲。

translations.literal: When Hailing heard of it, he often personally admonished him and forbade drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing repeatedly forbade it to his face.

sentences.zh: 得閒輒飲如故。

translations.literal: Given any leisure he drank as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the first chance he drank as before.

sentences.zh: 大定初，還自揚州，妻子為置酒私第，未數行，輒臥不飲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading, returning from Yangzhou, his wife set out wine in their private residence; before many rounds he lay down and would not drink.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading, home from Yangzhou, his wife poured wine in their private hall; after a few cups he lay down and refused more.

sentences.zh: 其妻大氏，海陵庶人從母姊也，怪而問之。
