translations.literal: His wife, Lady Da, was a cousin on Hailing the Commoner's mother's side. Surprised, she asked him why.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Da—a cousin on the deposed emperor Hailing's mother's side—asked what had changed.

sentences.zh: 昂曰：「吾本非嗜酒者，但向時不以酒自晦，則汝弟殺我久矣。

translations.literal: Ang said: "I am not a man who loves wine by nature, but had I not used wine to conceal myself in those days, your brother would have killed me long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Ang said, "I never loved wine for its own sake—but in those days, had I not drowned myself in it to seem harmless, your brother would have killed me long ago.

sentences.zh: 今遇遭明時，正當自愛，是以不飲。」

translations.literal: Now I have encountered an enlightened age and ought to cherish myself; that is why I do not drink."
translations.idiomatic: Now we live in an enlightened age. It is time to guard myself—that is why I abstain."

sentences.zh: 聞者稱之。

translations.literal: Those who heard it praised him.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard it praised his wisdom.

sentences.zh: 睦于兄弟，尤善施予，其親族有貧困者，必厚給之。

translations.literal: He was harmonious with his brothers and especially generous in giving; among his kinsmen, any who were in poverty he always enriched generously.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to his brothers and generous beyond measure; any needy kinsman he enriched without stint.

sentences.zh: 至於茵帳、衣衾、器皿、僕馬之屬，常預設於家。

translations.literal: As for bedding, coverlets, garments, quilts, vessels, servants, and horses and the like, he kept them constantly prepared at home.
translations.idiomatic: Bedding, clothes, vessels, servants, and horses he kept ready at home.

sentences.zh: 即命駕相就，為具，歡樂終日，盡以遺之，即日使富足。

translations.literal: He would at once have his carriage driven to visit them, provide a feast, and spend the day in gladness; he would give them everything and that same day make them prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: He would drive to their door, feast them through the day, and leave them everything—making them comfortable that same afternoon.

sentences.zh: 人或以子孫計為言，答曰：「人各有命，但使其能自立爾，何至為子孫奴耶？」

translations.literal: When some spoke of planning for posterity, he answered: "Each man has his own fate; one need only enable others to stand on their own—why reduce oneself to a slave for one's descendants?"
translations.idiomatic: When others urged him to think of his heirs, he answered, "Every man has his allotted span. Let them stand on their own feet—why make a slave of oneself for one's descendants?"

sentences.zh: 君子以為達。

translations.literal: Men of discernment regarded him as a man of insight.
translations.idiomatic: The wise counted him a man of true breadth.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：撒離喝、溫敦思忠、奔睹皆有功舊臣，當天會、皇統之際，戰勝攻取，可謂壯哉。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Saliha, Wendun Sizhong, and Bendu were all meritorious old ministers. In the eras of Tianhui and Huangtong, winning battles and taking cities—they were truly magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: Praise: Saliha, Wendun Sizhong, and Bendu were veterans who had earned their place. Through the Tianhui and Huangtong eras their victories were magnificent to behold.

sentences.zh: 及海陵之世，崎嶇嫌忌，撒離喝既自以言致疑，猶與大抃辨爭軍事，何見幾之不早也。

translations.literal: In Hailing's time, amid suspicion and peril, Saliha had already brought suspicion on himself by his words, yet still debated military affairs with Dabian—how slow he was to read the signs!
translations.idiomatic: Under Hailing, suspicion bred danger. Saliha had already invited distrust by his plain speaking, yet still wrangled with Dabian over military matters—how late he was to read the danger!

sentences.zh: 烏林答贊謨廉直自奮，思忠擠之於死，自謂固結海陵，堅若金石，豈意執議不合而遽棄耶。

translations.literal: Ulin Da Zanmo was upright and bold by nature. Sizhong hounded him to his death, yet Sizhong himself believed his bond with Hailing solid as metal and stone—who would have thought that when their views clashed he would be cast off so swiftly?
translations.idiomatic: Ulin Da Zanmo was upright and self-reliant; Sizhong drove him to his death. Sizhong believed his bond with Hailing firm as iron—yet when their counsel parted, he was cast aside overnight.

sentences.zh: 始之不以道，未有能終者也。

translations.literal: What begins without the Way has never been able to end well.
translations.idiomatic: What begins unjustly never ends well.

sentences.zh: 且思忠之最可罪者，構害贊謨，又納其室而敓其貲，此何異於殺越人於貨者乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, what most condemns Sizhong is that he framed Zanmo, then took his wife and seized his wealth—is this not the same as killing men for gain?
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong's worst crime was framing Zanmo, taking his wife, and seizing his fortune—is that not murder for profit?

sentences.zh: 陰報不在其身，在其子孫，亦已晚矣。

translations.literal: Though secret retribution did not fall on his own person, it fell on his descendants—and even that came late.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's vengeance skipped his person but found his descendants—though even that came late.

sentences.zh: 正隆之末，奔睹位三公，居上將，內不肯與謀，外不肯與戰，逼側趑趄，苟免自全，大臣之道，固若是乎？

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenglong, Bendu stood among the Three Dukes and held rank as a supreme general, yet within he would not join in counsel and without he would not join in battle—cramped and faltering, he merely saved himself. Is this how a great minister ought to be?
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhenglong, Bendu ranked among the Three Dukes and held supreme command—yet within he would not counsel, without he would not fight. Cringing and hesitating, he saved only himself. Is that the way of a great minister?

sentences.zh: 高楨，遼陽渤海人。

translations.literal: Gao Zhen was a man of Bohai in Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhen was a Bohai man of Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 五世祖牟翰仕遼，官至太師。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Mouhan served Liao and rose to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Mouhan had served the Liao and risen to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 楨少好學，嘗業進士。

translations.literal: Zhen from youth loved learning and once pursued the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen loved learning from youth and once pursued the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 斡魯討高永昌，已下沈州，永昌懼，偽送款以緩師。

translations.literal: Walu campaigned against Gao Yongchang. Having already taken Shenzhou, Yongchang was afraid and falsely sent tokens of submission to delay the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Walu marched against Gao Yongchang and had already taken Shenzhou, Yongchang feigned submission to slow the advance.

sentences.zh: 是時，楨母在沈州，遂來降，告以永昌降款非誠，斡魯乃進攻。

translations.literal: At that time Zhen's mother was in Shenzhou. She therefore came to surrender and reported that Yongchang's submission was insincere, whereupon Walu pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's mother was in Shenzhou; she came over and warned that Yongchang's surrender was a ruse, and Walu resumed the assault.

sentences.zh: 既破永昌，遂以楨同知東京留守事，授猛安。

translations.literal: After Yongchang was defeated, Zhen was made Associate Administrator of the Eastern Capital Garrison and granted a meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongchang's defeat, Zhen was made associate administrator of the Eastern Capital garrison and granted a meng'an.

sentences.zh: 天會六年，遷尚書左僕射，判廣甯尹，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhui he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, assigned as Administrator of Guangning, and given the additional title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhui he became Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and Administrator of Guangning, with the additional title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 在鎮八年，政令清肅，吏畏而人安之。

translations.literal: During eight years in his post, his orders were clear and strict; officials feared him and the people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years in office brought clear, stern government—officials feared him and the people were secure.

sentences.zh: 十五年，加太子太師，提點河北西路錢帛事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was given the additional title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and put in charge of cash and cloth on the Hebei West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and put in charge of currency and cloth on the Hebei West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 天眷初，同簽會寧牧。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjuan he jointly signed as Pastoral Lord of Huining.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianjuan he was appointed co-signatory Pastoral Lord of Huining.

sentences.zh: 及熙宗幸燕，兼同知留守，封戴國公，改同知燕京留守。

translations.literal: When the Xizong Emperor visited Yan, he was concurrently Associate Administrator of the Garrison, enfeoffed as Duke of Dai, and changed to Associate Administrator of the Yanjing Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong visited Yan, Zhen became associate garrison administrator, was enfeoffed Duke of Dai, and was transferred to associate administrator of the Yanjing garrison.

sentences.zh: 魏王道濟出守中京，以楨為同判，俄改行台平章政事，為西京留守，封任國公。

translations.literal: When Prince Wei Daoji went out to guard the Central Capital, Zhen was made Associate Administrator; soon he was changed to Grand Councilor of the Traveling Secretariat, made Garrison Commander of the Western Capital, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ren.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei Daoji took up the Central Capital, Zhen served as his associate administrator; soon he became grand councilor of the traveling secretariat, garrison commander of the Western Capital, and Duke of Ren.

sentences.zh: 是時，奚、嵆軍民皆南徙，謀克別術者因之嘯聚為盜。

translations.literal: At that time Xi and Ji civilians and soldiers had all moved south. The meng'an Bieshu thereupon gathered followers and became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xi and Ji people had all moved south; the meng'an Bieshu gathered followers and turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 海陵患之，即以楨為中京留守，命乘驛之官，責以平賊之期。

translations.literal: Hailing was troubled by this and immediately made Zhen Garrison Commander of the Central Capital, ordering him to take post by courier relay and fixing a deadline for suppressing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing appointed Zhen garrison commander of the Central Capital, ordered him to take post by relay horse, and set a deadline to crush the bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊平，封河內郡王。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were crushed, he was enfeoffed Prince of Henei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 海陵至中京，楨警夜嚴肅。

translations.literal: When Hailing reached the Central Capital, Zhen's night watches were strict and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing reached the Central Capital, Zhen kept the night watches in strict order.

sentences.zh: 有近侍馮僧家奴李街喜等皆得幸海陵，嘗夜飲幹禁，楨杖之瀕死，由是權貴皆震懾。

translations.literal: Palace attendants such as Feng Seng's household slave Li Jiexi and others had all won Hailing's favor. They once drank at night in violation of the curfew; Zhen beat them nearly to death, and from this the powerful all trembled in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants such as Feng Seng's slave Li Jiexi had won Hailing's favor. When they broke the night curfew to drink, Zhen beat them nearly to death—and from that day the mighty trembled before him.

sentences.zh: 遷太子太保，行御史大夫，封莒王。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, acted as Censor-in-Chief, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Ju.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and acting Censor-in-Chief, and enfeoffed Prince of Ju.

sentences.zh: 策拜司空，進封代王，太子太保、行御史大夫如故。

translations.literal: By proclamation he was appointed Minister of Works, advanced in enfeoffment to Prince of Dai, and his posts as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and acting Censor-in-Chief remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him Minister of Works and raised his fief to Prince of Dai; he kept his titles as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and acting Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 楨久在台，彈劾無所避，每進對，必以區別流品，進善退惡為言，當路者忌之。

translations.literal: Zhen had long served in the Censorate and impeached without shrinking from anyone. Whenever he appeared before the throne he always spoke of distinguishing ranks of men and promoting the good while removing the bad; those in power resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had long held office in the Censorate and impeached without fear. In every audience he urged the king to sort men by rank and promote virtue while casting out vice—and those in power came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 薦張忠輔、馬諷為中丞，二人皆險詖深刻，欲令以事中楨。

translations.literal: They recommended Zhang Zhongfu and Ma Feng as vice censors; both were devious, slanderous, and harsh, intending to have them find grounds to entrap Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed Zhang Zhongfu and Ma Feng for vice censor—both vicious men, sharp with slander—hoping they would find a way to ruin Zhen.

sentences.zh: 正隆例封冀國公，楨因固辭曰：「臣為眾小所嫉，恐不能免，尚可受封爵耶？」

translations.literal: By the Zhenglong precedent he was to be enfeoffed Duke of Ji. Zhen therefore firmly declined, saying: "Your subject is envied by many petty men and fears he cannot escape harm—how can he still accept a title and fief?"
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenglong precedent he was offered Duke of Ji. Zhen refused firmly: "Petty foes already hate me—I may not escape their malice. How can I accept a title?"

sentences.zh: 海陵知其忠直，慰而遣之。

translations.literal: Hailing knew his loyalty and integrity, comforted him, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing knew him upright and true, comforted him, and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 及疾革，書空獨語曰：「某事未決，某事未奏，死有餘恨。」

translations.literal: When his illness became critical, he traced characters in the air and spoke alone: "Such-and-such matters are undecided, such-and-such are unmemorialized—I will die with regrets remaining."
translations.idiomatic: When his illness turned grave, he traced words in the air and muttered alone: "This is unsettled, that unreported—I shall die with work undone."

sentences.zh: 薨，年六十九。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 海陵悼惜之，遣使致奠，賻贈加等。

translations.literal: Hailing mourned and regretted his loss, sent an envoy to offer sacrifice, and increased the funeral gifts and posthumous grants.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing mourned him, sent offerings, and enriched the funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 楨性方嚴，家居無聲伎之奉。

translations.literal: Zhen's character was upright and stern; at home he kept no musicians or entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was stern and upright; he kept no musicians or dancers at home.

sentences.zh: 雖甚暑，未嘗解衣緩帶。

translations.literal: Even in great heat he never loosened his belt or removed his outer robe.
translations.idiomatic: Even in sweltering heat he never loosened his belt or laid aside his robe.

sentences.zh: 對妻孥危坐終日，不一談笑，其簡默如此。

translations.literal: Facing his wife and children he sat upright all day long without a single jest—such was his restraint and silence.
translations.idiomatic: Before wife and children he sat bolt upright all day, never laughing or chatting—so spare and silent was he.

sentences.zh: 白彥敬

translations.literal: Bai Yanjing
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yanjing

sentences.zh: 白彥敬，本名遙設，部羅火部族人。

translations.literal: Bai Yanjing, original name Yaoshe, was a man of the Burahuo tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yanjing, born Yaoshe, belonged to the Burahuo tribe.

sentences.zh: 初名彥恭，避顯宗諱，改焉。

translations.literal: His name was originally Yangong; to avoid the taboo of the Xizong Emperor he changed it.
translations.idiomatic: He had first been named Yangong and changed it to avoid Emperor Xizong's taboo.

sentences.zh: 祖屋僕根。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Wupugen.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Wupugen.

sentences.zh: 父阿斯，仕遼為率府率。

translations.literal: His father Asi served Liao as Commandant of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Asi had served the Liao as commandant of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 彥敬善騎射，起家為吏，補元帥府令史。

translations.literal: Yanjing was skilled at horsemanship and archery. Beginning in office as a clerk, he was appointed marshalate recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjing excelled at riding and archery. He entered service as a clerk and was appointed recorder in the marshalate.

sentences.zh: 伐宋，為錢帛司都管勾。

translations.literal: During the campaign against Song he served as chief steward of the Bureau of Cash and Cloth.
translations.idiomatic: In the war on Song he became chief steward of the bureau of cash and cloth.

sentences.zh: 立三省，選為尚書省令史，除都元帥府知事。

translations.literal: When the Three Departments were established he was selected as recorder of the Department of State Affairs and appointed manager of the Grand Marshalate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Departments were set up he was chosen recorder of the Department of State Affairs and made manager of the grand marshalate.

sentences.zh: 招諭諸部，授以金牌，行數千里，有功，超遷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He was sent to win over the various tribes, granted gold credentials, and traveled several thousand li; for his merit he was promoted out of turn to director in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to win over the tribes with gold credentials, he rode thousands of li and won merit; he was promoted ahead of schedule to director in the bureau of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 熙宗罷統軍司改招討司，遣彥敬分僚屬改牌印，諭諸部隸招討司。

translations.literal: When the Xizong Emperor abolished the Military Affairs Commissions and replaced them with Pacification Commissions, he sent Yanjing to distribute the staff, change the seals and tallies, and instruct the tribes to come under the Pacification Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong replaced military commissions with pacification commissions, he sent Yanjing to reassign staffs, reissue seals, and bring the tribes under the new offices.

sentences.zh: 還為本部侍郎，遷大理卿，出為通州防禦使，改刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: On return he became vice director of his bureau, was transferred to Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, went out as defense commissioner of Tongzhou, and was changed to vice director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as vice director of his ministry, became chief judge of judicial review, served as defense commissioner of Tongzhou, and was transferred to vice director of the ministry of justice.

sentences.zh: 怨家告誣開府慎思與西北路部族謀叛，彥敬鞫得其實，海陵嘉之。

translations.literal: An enemy brought a false charge that Kaifu Shensi had plotted rebellion with Northwest Route tribes. Yanjing tried the case and found the truth; Hailing praised him.
translations.idiomatic: A personal enemy falsely accused Kaifu Shensi of plotting with Northwest Route tribes; Yanjing investigated, exposed the lie, and won Hailing's praise.

sentences.zh: 遷簽書樞密院事，以便宜措置邊防。

translations.literal: He was transferred to signed documents of the Bureau of Military Affairs and given discretionary authority to arrange the frontier defenses.
translations.idiomatic: He was made signing officer of the bureau of military affairs and empowered to settle frontier affairs as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 正隆六年，調諸路兵伐宋，及調民馬，使彥敬主會甯、蒲與、胡裏改三路事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenglong, when troops from all routes were mobilized for war on Song and civilian horses requisitioned, Yanjing was put in charge of affairs on the Ning, Puyu, and Huligai circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 6, when levies went out for war on Song and horses were requisitioned, Yanjing oversaw the Ning, Puyu, and Huligai circuits.

sentences.zh: 改吏部尚書，充南征萬戶，遷樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, made a southern-campaign wanhu, and transferred to vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of the ministry of personnel, a southern-campaign wanhu, and vice commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 契丹撒八反，樞密使僕散忽土等以無功坐誅，以彥敬為北面行營都統，與副統紇石烈志寧以便宜往，賜禦服皮襖。

translations.literal: When the Khitan Saba rebelled, Bureau Commissioner Pusan Hutu and others were executed for achieving nothing. Yanjing was made commander-in-chief of the Northern Route Field Headquarters; he and Vice Commander Hesheli Zhining were sent with discretionary authority and granted fur coats from the imperial wardrobe.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan Saba rose, Commissioner Pusan Hutu and others were executed for failure. Yanjing was named northern-route field commander; he and Vice Commander Hesheli Zhining marched with full discretion, each given an imperial fur coat.

sentences.zh: 行至北京，聞南征諸軍逃歸者皆奔東京，欲推戴世宗。

translations.literal: When they reached Beijing they heard that fugitives from the southern campaign armies had all fled to the Eastern Capital, intending to install Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: At Beijing they learned that deserters from the southern armies had gathered at the Eastern Capital to proclaim Shizong.

sentences.zh: 彥敬與志甯謀，陰結會甯尹完顏蒲速賚、利涉軍節度使獨吉義以圖之。

translations.literal: Yanjing and Zhining plotted together and secretly enlisted Huining Intendant Wanyan Pusai and Lishes Army Military Commissioner Duji Yi to join their design.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjing and Zhining plotted in secret, winning Huining intendant Wanyan Pusai and Lishes Army commissioner Duji Yi to their cause.

sentences.zh: 世宗已即位，使石抹移迭、移剌曷補等九人招彥敬、志寧。

translations.literal: Shizong had already ascended the throne and sent nine men including Shim Tan Yidie and Yelü Hebu to win over Yanjing and Zhining.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong, already enthroned, sent nine envoys—among them Shim Tan Yidie and Yelü Hebu—to win Yanjing and Zhining over.

sentences.zh: 彥敬拒之，使移迭跪。

translations.literal: Yanjing refused them and made Yidie kneel.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjing refused and ordered Yidie to kneel.

sentences.zh: 移迭不屈，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Yidie would not submit; he killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Yidie would not yield, Yanjing had them all killed.

sentences.zh: 及完顏謀衍將兵攻北京，彥敬使偏將率兵拒於建州之境，而獨吉義先歸世宗，蒲速賚稱疾不至。

translations.literal: When Wanyan Mouyan led troops to attack Beijing, Yanjing sent a lieutenant general with troops to hold the border of Jianzhou; but Duji Yi had already gone over to Shizong, and Pusai claimed illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanyan Mouyan marched on Beijing, Yanjing sent a lieutenant to block him at Jianzhou—but Duji Yi had already joined Shizong, and Pusai pleaded illness and never came.

sentences.zh: 世宗密遣人乘夜揭榜於北京市，購以官賞。

translations.literal: Shizong secretly sent men who by night posted proclamations in the Beijing market, offering official rewards as the price.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong secretly posted night proclamations in the Beijing market, promising office and reward.

sentences.zh: 彥敬、志甯恐為人圖己，遂降。

translations.literal: Yanjing and Zhining, fearing others would plot against them, thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing betrayal, Yanjing and Zhining surrendered.

sentences.zh: 以為曷速館節度使。

translations.literal: He was made military commissioner of Yisuguan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjing was made commissioner of Yisuguan.

sentences.zh: 不數月，召為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Within a few months he was summoned and made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was recalled as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 窩斡忄栗帝號。

translations.literal: Wohe usurped an imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: Wohe declared himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 諸軍馬瘦弱，遣彥敬往西北路招討司市馬，得六千餘匹。

translations.literal: The horses of the armies were weak and thin; Yanjing was sent to the Northwest Route Pacification Commission to purchase horses and obtained more than six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The army's horses were failing; Yanjing was sent to the Northwest Route pacification commission to buy mounts and returned with more than six thousand.

sentences.zh: 窩斡敗，西走山后。

translations.literal: Wohe was defeated and fled west into the lands beyond the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, Wohe fled west into the northern hills.

sentences.zh: 完顏思敬以新馬三千備追襲。

translations.literal: Wanyan Sijin took three thousand fresh horses to prepare for pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Sijin readied three thousand fresh horses for the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 彥敬屯于夏國兩界間。

translations.literal: Yanjing encamped between the borders of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjing camped on the borderlands between Jin and Xia.

sentences.zh: 窩斡平，召還為兵部尚書，出為鳳翔尹，改太原尹，兼河北東路兵馬總管，尋改河中尹。

translations.literal: When Wohe was pacified he was recalled and made Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, went out as Intendant of Fengxiang, was changed to Intendant of Taiyuan and concurrently commander of Hebei East Route troops and horses, and soon changed to Intendant of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: After Wohe's defeat he returned as director of the bureau of military affairs, served as intendant of Fengxiang and then Taiyuan, commanded Hebei East Route forces, and soon became intendant of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 大定九年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dading he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 9 he died in office.

sentences.zh: 張景仁

translations.literal: Zhang Jingren
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingren

sentences.zh: 張景仁，字壽甫，遼西人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingren, courtesy name Shoufu, was a man of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingren, courtesy name Shoufu, came from Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 累官翰林待制。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he reached Hanlin Attendant Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through service to Hanlin attendant drafter.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，與翟永固俱試禮部進士，以「尊祖配天」為賦題，忤海陵旨，語在永固傳。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan he and Zhai Yonggu both sat for the Ministry of Rites jinshi examination with the fu topic "Honoring the Ancestor and Pairing Him with Heaven"; they ran counter to Hailing's intent—the account is in Yonggu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 2 he and Zhai Yonggu took the jinshi examination with the topic "Honoring the Ancestor, Pairing Him with Heaven"; they offended Hailing—the story is told in Yonggu's biography.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，僕散忠義伐宋，景仁掌其文辭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading, when Pusan Zhongyi campaigned against Song, Jingren handled its documents and dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 2, when Pusan Zhongyi warred on Song, Jingren drafted the correspondence.

sentences.zh: 宋人議和，朝廷已改奉表為國書，稱臣為侄，但不肯世稱侄國。

translations.literal: When the Song sought peace, the court had already changed the submitting memorial into a state letter, calling itself nephew to the other as uncle, but refused to be forever known as a nephew state.
translations.idiomatic: In peace talks the court had replaced tribute memorials with state letters, accepting the name "nephew" to Jin's "uncle"—but would not be forever called a nephew state.

sentences.zh: 往復凡七書，然後定，其書皆景仁為之。

translations.literal: Seven letters passed back and forth before terms were fixed, and Jingren wrote them all.
translations.idiomatic: Seven letters went back and forth before terms were set—all in Jingren's hand.

sentences.zh: 世宗稱其能，嘗曰：「今之文章，如張景仁與宋人往復書，指事達意，辨而裁，真能文之士也。」

translations.literal: Shizong praised his ability and once said: "Among writers today, men like Zhang Jingren in his letters exchanged with Song—addressing each matter, conveying intent, discriminating and cutting to the point—are truly capable with words."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong praised him: "Writers today? Look at Zhang Jingren's letters to Song—clear, precise, discriminating. That is real literary craft."

sentences.zh: 五年，罷兵，入為翰林直學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year hostilities ceased and he entered court as Direct Academician of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year peace came; he entered court as Hanlin direct academician.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷侍講。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Court Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became court lecturer.

sentences.zh: 八年，為詳讀官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he became detailed-reading officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became a detailed-reading officer.

sentences.zh: 宋國書中有「寶鄰」字，景仁奏「鄰」字太涉平易。

translations.literal: In a Song state letter there was the phrase "precious neighbor"; Jingren memorialized that the character for "neighbor" was too plain and easy.
translations.idiomatic: A Song letter used the phrase "precious neighbor"; Jingren protested that "neighbor" was too plain a word.

sentences.zh: 上問累年國書有「鄰」字否，命一一校勘。

translations.literal: The emperor asked whether state letters in successive years had the character for "neighbor" and ordered them checked one by one.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked whether earlier state letters had used that word and ordered a line-by-line review.

sentences.zh: 六年書中亦有之，上責問六年詳讀官劉仲淵，右丞石琚亦請罪曰：「臣嘗預六年詳讀。」

translations.literal: The letter of the sixth year also had it. The emperor rebuked Liu Zhongyuan, the detailed-reading officer of that year; Right Vice Director Shi Ju also asked punishment, saying: "Your subject once took part in the sixth-year detailed reading."
translations.idiomatic: The sixth-year letter contained it too. The emperor rebuked Liu Zhongyuan, who had read that year; Vice Director Shi Ju also asked punishment: "I took part in that reading."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此有司之過，安得一一責宰臣邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is the fault of the offices concerned—how can every minister be blamed?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is the clerks' fault—why blame every minister?"

sentences.zh: 詔有司就諭宋臣王瀹，使歸告其主，後日國書不得複爾。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the responsible offices to instruct the Song official Wang Yue on the spot, that he return and report to his lord that hereafter state letters must not again be so.
translations.idiomatic: An edict told the offices to inform Song minister Wang Yue: report to your sovereign that such wording must not appear again.

sentences.zh: 仲淵時為禮部侍郎，降石州刺史，景仁遷翰林學士兼同修國史。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan was at the time Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites; he was demoted to Prefect of Shizhou. Jingren was transferred to Hanlin Academician and concurrently compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan, then vice director of rites, was demoted to prefect of Shizhou; Jingren became Hanlin academician and co-compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 久之，上召景仁讀陳言文字。

translations.literal: After some time the emperor summoned Jingren to read memorials of candid speech.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor had Jingren read submitted memorials aloud.

sentences.zh: 上問「事款幾何？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "How many items are there?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "How many items?"

sentences.zh: 景仁率易，少周密，對曰：「二十餘事。」

translations.literal: Jingren was careless and casual, not very thorough; he answered: "More than twenty items."
translations.idiomatic: Jingren, careless and loose, answered: "More than twenty."

sentences.zh: 複曰：「其中如某事某事十事可行，餘皆無謂也。」

translations.literal: He added: "Among them, such-and-such ten items are workable; the rest are all pointless."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Ten or so are workable; the rest are worthless."

sentences.zh: 明日，上召景仁責之曰：「卿昨言可行者，朕觀之，中複有不可行者。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor summoned Jingren and rebuked him: "Yesterday you said certain items were workable; I have looked, and among them some cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the emperor rebuked him: "Yesterday you called some items workable—I find some cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 卿謂無謂者，中亦有可行者。

translations.literal: Those you called pointless also contain items that can be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: And items you dismissed also contain workable proposals.

sentences.zh: 朕未嘗使卿分別可否，卿輒專可否，何也？

translations.literal: I never told you to judge what is workable and what is not—why did you on your own authority divide them so?
translations.idiomatic: I never asked you to judge them—why did you decide on your own?

sentences.zh: 自今戒之。」

translations.literal: From now on be warned."
translations.idiomatic: See that you do not again."

sentences.zh: 十年，兼太常卿，學士、同修國史如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was given the additional post of Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his posts as academician and co-compiler of the National History remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he also became director of imperial sacrifices, keeping his posts as academician and co-compiler.

sentences.zh: 轉承旨，兼修國史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Academician Expositor and given the additional charge of compiling the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He became expositor and was charged with compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 改河南尹。

translations.literal: He was changed to Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，召為御史大夫，仍兼承旨、修國史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was summoned and made Censor-in-Chief, still concurrently expositor and compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was recalled as censor-in-chief, still expositor and history compiler.

sentences.zh: 世宗謂景仁曰：「卿博學老儒，求如古之御史大夫，然後行之，期為稱矣。

translations.literal: Shizong said to Jingren: "You are a learned elder of the Confucian school. I want you to be like the censor-in-chief of old—only then will the appointment be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong told Jingren: "You are a learned elder. Be the censor-in-chief of antiquity—then the office will suit you.

sentences.zh: 不能如古之人，眾人不獨誚卿，亦謂朕不能知人。

translations.literal: If you cannot be like the men of old, people will not only mock you—they will say I cannot judge men.
translations.idiomatic: Fall short of that, and men will blame not only you but my judgment as well.

sentences.zh: 卿醉中頗輕脫失言，當以酒為戒。」

translations.literal: When drunk you are rather careless and loose-tongued; you must take wine as your warning."
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, you are loose with your tongue—let wine be your warning."

sentences.zh: 初，朝臣言景仁有文藝而頗率易，不可任台察。

translations.literal: At first court officials had said Jingren had literary talent but was rather casual and could not hold censorial office.
translations.idiomatic: At first courtiers had said Jingren was talented but too casual for the censorate.

sentences.zh: 景仁被詔，就台中治監察罪，輒以便服視決罰。

translations.literal: When Jingren received the edict he tried censorial cases within the Censorate and casually watched punishments being carried out in ordinary dress.
translations.idiomatic: After his appointment he tried censorial cases at the yamen and watched punishments in ordinary dress.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，責景仁曰：「朕初用卿為大夫，或言卿不可居此官，今果不用故事，率易如此。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he rebuked Jingren: "When I first used you as censor-in-chief, some said you could not hold this office—and now, sure enough, you ignore precedent and are this casual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him: "When I named you censor-in-chief, some warned you were unfit—and now you ignore precedent and dress like this.

sentences.zh: 卿自慎，不然黜罰及矣！」

translations.literal: Be careful yourself—otherwise demotion and punishment will reach you!"
translations.idiomatic: Guard yourself—or demotion will follow!"

sentences.zh: 景仁頓首謝。

translations.literal: Jingren kowtowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren kowtowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔葬元妃李氏于海王莊。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered the burial of Consort Li in Prince of the Sea's Villa.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered Consort Li buried at Prince of the Sea's Villa.

sentences.zh: 平章政事烏古論元忠提控葬事，都水監丞高杲壽治道路不如式，元忠不奏，決之四十。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Wugulun Yuanzhong oversaw the burial. Director of Waterways Assistant Gao Gaoshou maintained the road contrary to regulation; Yuanzhong did not memorialize it but had him beaten forty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Wugulun Yuanzhong oversaw the burial. Assistant director Gao Gaoshou's roadwork fell short of standard; Yuanzhong did not report it but had him beaten forty strokes.

sentences.zh: 景仁劾奏元忠輒斷六品官，無人臣禮。

translations.literal: Jingren impeached Yuanzhong for arbitrarily deciding punishment on a sixth-rank official and lacking the propriety of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren impeached Yuanzhong for beating a sixth-rank official without proper procedure—a minister's disregard of court form.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿劾奏甚當。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your impeachment is very fitting."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Your impeachment is just."

sentences.zh: 使左宣徽使蒲察鼎壽傳詔戒敕元忠曰：「監丞六品，有罪聞奏，今乃一切趨辦，擅決六品官，法當如是耶？

translations.literal: He had Left Commissioner of the Palace Attendants' Office Pucha Dingshou transmit an edict of admonition to Yuanzhong: "An assistant director is sixth rank; if guilty it should be reported. Now everything is rushed to completion and you on your own authority decide punishment for a sixth-rank official—is that what the law provides?
translations.idiomatic: He sent Commissioner Pucha Dingshou to admonish Yuanzhong: "A sixth-rank official who offends should be reported. You rushed the work and took punishment into your own hands—is that the law?

sentences.zh: 禦史在尊朝廷，汝當自咎，勿複再！」

translations.literal: The censor exists to honor the court—you should blame yourself; do not do this again!"
translations.idiomatic: The censor exists to uphold the court. Blame yourself—and do not repeat this."

sentences.zh: 元忠尚豫國公主，怙寵自任，倨慢朝士。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong had married the Princess of Yugu; relying on favor he did as he pleased and was haughty toward court officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong had married the Princess of Yugu; pampered by favor, he was haughty toward his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 景仁劾之，朝廷肅然。

translations.literal: Jingren impeached him, and the court grew stern and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren impeached him again, and the court fell silent with respect.

sentences.zh: 是歲，薨。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：高楨以舊勞為御史大夫，剛明自任，繩治無所避，幾不免於怨憎之荼毒。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Gao Zhen, by virtue of old service, became Censor-in-Chief; upright and clear in his own conduct, in imposing discipline he shrank from nothing and nearly did not escape the bitter poison of enmity and hatred.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Gao Zhen won the censorate through long service—upright, self-possessed, punishing without fear—and barely escaped the poison of resentment.

sentences.zh: 直己而行，自古難之。

translations.literal: To act straight according to oneself has from antiquity been hard.
translations.idiomatic: To walk straight by one's own light has always been hard.

sentences.zh: 白彥敬不受大定之詔而世宗賢之。

translations.literal: Bai Yanjing did not accept Shizong's summons at the beginning of Dading, yet Shizong considered him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yanjing first refused Shizong's summons, yet the emperor held him worthy.

sentences.zh: 向使久在此位，其深謀讜論，必有竦動人者。

translations.literal: Had he long remained in this office, his deep counsel and forthright discourse would surely have stirred men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Had he kept the post longer, his counsel would surely have moved the realm.

sentences.zh: 張景仁儒者之勇，廷論元忠，正矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingren had the courage of a Confucian scholar; in court debate over Yuanzhong he was correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingren had a scholar's courage—his attack on Yuanzhong in open court was right.
